title: A Technique for Load Shifting Low-latency Applications in Multi-Region Renewables Harvesting via SMT Core Pooling
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / cloud scheduling / sustainable systems
why: Hardware-software co-design for renewable-aware multi-region load shifting of low-latency workloads. Implemented with OpenStack and CPU idle states on a real testbed using Azure VM arrival traces; results report 80% less offloading of low-latency VMs and 43.81% lower coefficient of variation of p90 end-user latency, with 11.97% worst-case latency compromise from SMT. This is direct measured systems evidence.

title: A Time-Encoded Analog Photonic Interposer for Energy-EfficientIntegration of Analog Vision Sensors and Analog Accelerators
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / photonic interconnect / analog AI accelerator
why: A time-encoded analog photonic interposer transports analog vision signals between chiplets without a conventional high-precision ADC/DAC pipeline. The primary abstract reports a 2.04x energy-delay-product improvement over an 8-bit digital electrical baseline on Visual Wake Words while keeping accuracy close to the digital baseline.

title: A Universal Context-Reuse Layer for Cross-Model KV Sharing
topic: KV cache / LLM serving / cross-model context reuse / multi-agent inference
why: Introduces cross-model KV sharing across different model scales, architectures, attention configurations, tokenizers and families. Reports up to 67.05% target-side prefill reduction at 4K context and a Llama3.1-70B to Qwen2.5-7B handoff reducing measured latency from 899 ms to 138 ms with near-native accuracy.

title: A*-Thought-V2: Efficient Latent Reasoning via Geometric Dynamics of LLM
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / latent reasoning / token compression / efficient training
why: Interleaves explicit text with pooled continuous latent tokens using geometric trajectory alignment. Across Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-27B it improves average accuracy by up to 2.6% while cutting response length by up to half, raising Accuracy per Computation Unit by 2.29x, and reducing preprocessing/training time by 94.6%/up to 80.3%.

title: A1: A Fully Transparent Open-Source, Adaptive and Efficient Truncated Vision-Language-Action Model
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive early exit / flow action-head acceleration
why: Protected Physical-AI efficiency gap. Budget-aware adaptive VLM early termination plus inter-layer truncated flow matching jointly accelerate backbone and action head; reports up to 72% lower per-episode flow-matching latency and 76.6% backbone compute reduction. Full official training stack is open source.

title: Accelerating Diffusion Transformers with Gaussian Process Rectified Feature Cache
topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / feature caching / adaptive compute
why: ECCV 2026 plug-and-play GP-Refiner corrects prediction-based feature caches with Gaussian-process uncertainty and adaptively triggers full-compute calibration. Combined with TaylorSeer it reduces computational load by 19.3% while improving PSNR by 0.9 dB and reducing LPIPS from 0.46 to 0.29, giving a direct quality-efficiency improvement.

title: AccelMPC: High-Rate, Low-Power FPGA-Accelerated Model Predictive Control for Tiny Drones
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge robotics / FPGA acceleration / real-time control
why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-system co-design spanning MPC solver algorithm, numerical representation, FPGA mapping and physical integration on a 35g Crazyflie. Hardware experiments demonstrate 1 kHz onboard constrained MPC with dynamic obstacles, up to 15.6x faster solve times and 195.4x better energy-delay product than state-of-the-art embedded microcontroller solvers, scaling beyond 20,000 variables and constraints; PCB, firmware and FPGA code are open source.

title: ACE: Adapter Consolidation across Experts for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of MoE LLMs
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / distributed training / PEFT
why: ACE consolidates redundant expert-specific LoRA adapters into group-shared higher-rank adapters and executes them as fewer larger GEMMs. Across four MoE backbones it provides 1.31-1.48x wall-clock training speedup over expert-wise LoRA without increasing peak memory.

title: ActionCache: Training-Free Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Models with Action Caching and Refinement
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / action cache / flow action-head acceleration
why: Training-free external action cache reuses retrieved intermediate actions to warm-start flow/diffusion action generation, directly reducing iterative action-head NFEs and latency for pi0.5 and GR00T-N1.6.

title: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / interactive world models / inference runtime
why: ActionSplice transports the interrupted backbone-native state to the revised-action state without rolling back completed solver evaluations. Across minWM-Wan Action2V and HY-WM1.5, temporal splicing provides 2.73x and 1.69x pixel-ready speedups over waiting while substantially reducing rollback-relative perceptual error.

title: Adaptive Context Parallelism for Production LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / context parallelism / adaptive placement / prefix cache / cluster reconfiguration
why: 30d distributed-serving replay recovered a direct production LLM serving paper absent from authority. Vertumnus routes requests among workers with different context-parallel degrees using queueing, cache-aware prefill, and GPU-time cost; it also performs seconds-scale split/merge reconfiguration and global prefix-cache coordination. A 64-GPU evaluation reports up to 28.1% lower mean TTFT and +13.3 percentage points token-weighted SLO attainment.

title: Aero Realtime: Fully Aligned Input-Output Streams for Low-Latency Streaming Multimodal Generation
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming generation / KV reuse / distributed training
why: True 30d systems miss. Aero Realtime replaces turn-based prefill-then-decode with a duplex slot-aligned streaming architecture in which new multimodal observations and text generation advance together. Inference appends only the newest slot and reuses KV cache; the work also includes a serving recipe, hardware-aware distributed training and resumable inference. On four A6000 GPUs it reports 84 ms median and 173 ms P95 processing lag over a 20-minute continuous stream, making this directly relevant to realtime multimodal serving/runtime rather than only model quality.

title: Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / autonomous algorithm engineering / shared-memory optimization / performance tuning
why: Autonomous LLM agents repeatedly profile, modify and benchmark an already heavily hand-tuned shared-memory exact minimum-cut implementation. The resulting changes yield 1.28x sequential and 1.63x 32-thread speedups on real-world k-cores, and 6.26x/127x on DIMACS core instances, providing direct measured evidence that agentic systems can improve low-level algorithm/runtime efficiency rather than only generate code.

title: AInfer-PD: Communication-Safe In-Place Prefill-Decode Multiplexing for Distributed MoE Rollouts
topic: LLM serving / agentic RL rollout / prefill-decode multiplexing / distributed MoE / communication
why: Extends in-place P/D multiplexing to distributed MoE rollout inference with coordinated collective ordering and independent DeepEP communication state. Reports 7.1-22.5% lower fixed-workload completion time than the same AInfer engine without multiplexing and 24.8-32.9% versus SGLang on single-node workloads; two-node reductions are 18.0-35.3% and 18.3-31.8%.

title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
topic: quantization / LLM inference / genuine 1-bit PTQ
why: AF1 targets a strict 1.0-BPW post-training quantization budget rather than nominal binary weights with hidden overhead. On LLaMA/Qwen/Gemma it reports better quality than prior binarization PTQ, average 2.5x inference speedup versus BF16 and over 90% memory reduction, with reproducible code.

title: Almost Free State Prediction Separation
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / LLM inference / KV-cache-neutral extra compute
why: Microsoft/Cornell free-pause-token method improves next-token prediction by 2-3 centinats on a 1B model while adding no context length, no KV cache, and essentially no inference latency; training overhead is reduced to about 1.14x. This is directly relevant to inference-efficient extra-compute/reasoning design.

title: Ambient @ EgoLongQA 2026: Distilling Long-Video perception into a Sub-2B Model
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / model compression / video reasoning
why: A sub-2B VLM distills the perception component of a larger tool-using long-video agent into one greedy forward pass. It retains 89% of the large agent pipeline accuracy while using only 1.1% of its parameters, providing unusually strong model-size and deployment-efficiency evidence for long-video reasoning.

title: AMEND: Audited Margins Enable Nonblocking Drops in GPU-PIM LLM Decoding
topic: KV cache/long-context / sparse attention / GPU-PIM / LLM decoding
why: Predicts block-sparse attention decisions from audited prior-step margins so the GPU fetches only predicted survivors while near-bank PIM concurrently checks omitted blocks, avoiding a serial selector on the token critical path. Across LongBench/RULER simulation at batch 8 it preserves near-baseline quality and reports 1.40-3.63x end-to-end decode speedup with 28-66% lower dynamic decode energy over 8K-64K contexts.

title: An Efficient Out-of-Core Tomographic Imaging Framework for Edge Devices
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / GPU kernel / mixed precision / out-of-core
why: edgeFBP is an end-to-end out-of-core CT reconstruction runtime for Nvidia Jetson SoCs using mixed precision and Tensor Cores for the bottleneck back-projection kernel. It reports 1.83x speedup over RTK on Jetson Nano, 2.56x on Jetson AGX, and up to 5-48x higher energy efficiency than DGX A100 under a 25W budget, giving direct measured edge-system evidence.

title: Analytical Resource Management for Fine-grained MoE Computation-Communication Overlap
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / distributed inference / compute-communication overlap
why: A wave-quantized analytical model selects communication CTA count and SM-resource partition before launch for dependency-coupled MoE overlap. Integrated into COMET/FLUX on four A100 GPUs, it reports 2.528x geometric-mean speedup at GEMM2+GatherRS, 1.771x at the post-router MoE layer, and 1.185x complete-model prefill versus COMET, with 0.157 us mean solver overhead.

title: AnchorKV: Anchor-Residual KV Cache Compression
topic: KV cache/long-context / compression
why: Direct KV-cache compression retaining all tokens via anchors plus selective residual refinement; reports 20x cache compression while retaining 99% of full-cache score at 70B scale.

title: Archer: Adaptive Reuse of Cached Hidden States for Efficient Rollback in Diffusion Language Models
topic: KV cache / diffusion language model acceleration
why: Training-free KV/hidden-state reuse aligned to rollback-capable diffusion language models. Reports 2.57x mean speedup on the main suite, up to 2.95x speedup, while improving mean task performance.

title: Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / edge-cloud AI infrastructure
why: Microsoft Azure production characterization of agentic workloads and server architecture. Identifies CPU-GPU fragmentation, burstiness and heterogeneous orchestration roles; Agora improves utilization/server throughput while preserving agent tail latency.

title: ASTRA: Low-Overhead Runtime Architecture for STReam Adaptation in Video Analytics
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / multimodal serving / runtime adaptation
why: ASTRA is a low-overhead runtime for online resolution/frame-rate adaptation in live edge video analytics, deployed on the NSF COSMOS testbed and evaluated with up to eight cameras under real network conditions. It maintains over 90% probability of meeting accuracy/latency requirements, stays within 10% of offline-optimal performance, and adds about 2% average GPU-utilization overhead per camera.

title: AstraFlow: Dataflow-Oriented Reinforcement Learning for Agentic LLMs
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / distributed RL training / heterogeneous elastic execution
why: Direct agentic-RL system: dataflow-oriented rollout/training decoupling, multi-policy collaboration, elastic heterogeneous cross-region execution; reports 2.7x training-time speedup and <=1.1% sparse weight-delta transfer in the official project evidence.

title: Atlas: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design for On-Device City-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting in VR
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / 3D Gaussian splatting / on-device rendering
why: Direct algorithm-hardware/runtime co-design for memory-constrained on-device 3DGS. Hierarchical offloading, temporal-aware LoD search and stereo rasterization yield 18.5x speedup over GPU baseline, 3.9x over prior 3DGS accelerators and 92.4% energy savings.

title: Atlas: Optimizing Deployment of Compound AI Workflows on Heterogeneous Clusters
topic: distributed inference / compound AI serving / heterogeneous clusters / SLO-aware deployment optimization
why: 30d distributed-inference replay recovered a systems paper absent from authority. Atlas predicts workflow-level accuracy from local conditional transitions, composes this with system profiles, and solves model-variant plus heterogeneous-hardware placement under SLO constraints; across four workflows it reports up to 0.947 Spearman correlation, 2.6x lower profiling cost than exhaustive profiling, and up to 42% lower deployment cost while matching oracle accuracy.

title: AttnCompress: Dynamic Attention-Guided Trajectory Compression for Software Engineering Agents
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / context compression / agent serving
why: ISSTA 2026 dynamic trajectory compression uses structure-aware segmentation, proxy-attention relevance, and a rolling recall window. On SWE-Bench-Verified and Multi-SWE-Bench it reaches 53.17% pass rate while cutting token consumption by 21.6% and total cost by 33.6%, a measured agent-serving efficiency gain without sacrificing task quality.

title: AuK Technical Report: An Open-Source Foundational Model for Speech Generation and Editing
topic: multimodal generative inference / flow distillation / low-step generation
why: Distills a rectified-flow speech generation/editing foundation model with consistency initialization and task-routed Decoupled DMD. AuK-Flash performs 4-step inference without classifier-free guidance and reports 4.5x wall-clock speedup over the full model under matched conditions, while retaining leading/competitive generation and editing quality.

title: AutoUVM: Automated Prefetching Framework for LLMs under UVM Oversubscription
topic: LLM serving / memory oversubscription / UVM prefetching / heterogeneous memory
why: Framework-aware transparent UVM prefetching exposes tensor-level access information and dynamically adapts to memory pressure. Across ten LLMs it reports 3.1x average speedup over baseline UVM, 1.9x over the best prior UVM prefetcher, and up to 4.7x over object-level prefetchers while reducing page faults.

title: BaseRT: Advancing Best-in-Class LLM Inference with Apple M5 Neural Accelerators
topic: edge/on-device LLM inference; Apple M5 neural accelerators; Metal 4 tensor kernels; MoE; attention
why: Distinct BaseRT hardware-generation paper: hand-written Metal 4 tensor-core dense/MoE GEMM and flash-attention kernels for M5 neural accelerators; reports up to 6.4x prompt-processing throughput over llama.cpp and 3.9x over MLX, with decode gains retained.

title: BaseRT: Best-in-Class LLM Inference on Apple Silicon via Native Metal
topic: edge/on-device LLM inference runtime; Apple Silicon; Metal kernels; quantization
why: Apple-Silicon native-runtime canonical gap: framework-free Metal runtime with chip-specific kernel fusion, unified-memory-aware optimization and custom dispatch; supports Q2-FP16 and reports up to 1.56x decode throughput over llama.cpp and 1.35x over MLX.

title: BASP: Communication-Efficient Batch-Aware Sequence Parallelism for LLM Training
topic: distributed training/inference / long-context training / sequence parallelism
why: Direct distributed-training systems technique: batch-aware GPU grouping reduces all-to-all group size for sequence parallelism. A100-cluster experiments report 1.17-1.31x end-to-end training-time improvement for Llama/Qwen while preserving accuracy and memory usage.

title: BF16 Component-Product Emulation of FP32 and FP64 GEMM on Intel AMX
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / CPU matrix engines / low-precision GEMM / Intel AMX
why: 7d replay recovered a systems method that uses BF16 AMX component products to emulate higher-precision FP32/FP64 GEMM. The implementation uses packed BF16 components, VNNI-packed panels and tile-resident operand reuse; tested configurations can exceed oneMKL SGEMM and, at sufficiently large orders and low product counts, oneMKL DGEMM. This is directly relevant to low-precision matrix-engine utilization for higher-precision workloads.

title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving
topic: Physical AI / WAM / autonomous driving / asynchronous rectified-flow inference / action-space coordination
why: Protected 30d Physical-AI/WAM replay recovered a direct inference-efficiency mechanism absent from authority/watch. BrainWAM keeps semantic VLA priors and predictive world dynamics in specialized action-oriented pathways, then introduces asynchronous rectified-flow inference that decouples video and action denoising to shorten inference latency while preserving planning-relevant predictive context.

title: CacheBridge: Efficient Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer
topic: KV cache / multi-model serving / GPU kernel
why: Cross-model KV transfer with matched-head affine mapping, attention-aware calibration and fused GPU sufficient-statistics kernel; reports 8x lower mapper storage, up to 3.0x application speedup and 10.7x faster mapper construction while retaining target quality.

title: CacheFlow: Efficient LLM Serving with 3D-Parallel KV Cache Restoration
topic: LLM serving; KV-cache restoration; long-context inference; token/layer/GPU parallelism; compute-I/O overlap
why: Fresh major-group saturation recheck of the UIUC Fan Lai lineage surfaced a true paper-level miss. CacheFlow reframes KV restoration as 3D parallel execution across tokens, layers and GPUs with batch-aware scheduling to overlap recomputation and I/O; the paper reports 10%-62% TTFT reduction over existing restoration methods across long-context serving workloads.

title: CAKE: Compiler-Agent Co-Design for Frontier Kernel Evolution
topic: GPU kernel / DSL / compiler / agentic systems / LLM serving
why: Compiler-agent co-design exposes hardware-explicit scheduling through CAKE IR and closes the loop between agent failures and compiler evolution. On B200 the best candidate exceeds tuned FlashML on Flash-KMeans; agent-generated Kimi Delta Attention reports 2.05x geometric-mean speedup over official FlashKDA and passes end-to-end serving validation. Directly relevant to GPU-kernel/DSL/compiler and AI-infra automation.

title: CEDAR: Error-Bounded Residual Routing for Efficient Long-Context Attention
topic: efficient attention / long context / sparse routing / kernel acceleration
why: CEDAR combines chunk summaries with error-aware exact refinement instead of hard-dropping omitted chunks, preserving global coverage with a variable refinement budget. The primary abstract reports over 98% reconstruction-error reduction versus hard dropping at equal exact-chunk budgets and approximately 3x kernel speedup at 128K context.

title: CIERA: Cross-Iteration Exponent Reuse for Lossless Allgather in Sharded MoE Training
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / distributed training / lossless allgather compression
why: Direct system-aware MoE communication method. Caches stable exponents across iterations, transmits sign+mantissa when safe, overlaps compression with Allgather/computation, preserves bitwise-exact reconstruction, and reports 3.70x speedup at 16 GPUs with 4.28x projected at 128 GPUs.

title: CLFTv2: Efficient Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Semantic Segmentation via Hierarchical Feature Pyramids
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / multimodal perception / efficient attention / edge inference
why: Replaces global ViT/query-matching fusion with hierarchical shifted-window attention and a lightweight FPN-style decoder. Against a Swin-based Mask2Former adaptation it uses 1.4x fewer GFLOPs and delivers 2.2x higher throughput with comparable overall accuracy while improving vulnerable-road-user recall, giving direct on-vehicle perception efficiency evidence.

title: CMD: An Integrated CGRA Framework with Cluster-Based Distributed Memory Design
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / accelerators / CGRA / memory-aware compilation
why: 7d systematic replay recovered an integrated reconfigurable-accelerator framework with co-designed memory-aware compiler and design-space exploration. Post-DSE CMD CGRAs report 1.39x average speedup over a conventional CGRA while reducing total area to 0.912x on average, providing measured architecture/compiler efficiency evidence.

title: Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent topology / inference cost
why: Codebook Agent amortizes per-query multi-agent communication-topology search into a compact learned codebook and batched MLP reranker. Across six benchmarks it emits a topology in 2.4 ms, improves average accuracy over prior designers, and uses 21.9-33.2% fewer LLM tokens, providing direct systems evidence for cheaper agent orchestration.

title: CoFiE: Coarse-to-Fine Evidence Selection for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparsity / streaming video
why: Moves coarse evidence filtering before the expensive vision encoder, then performs query-specific refinement at LLM prefill. Reports up to 80% evidence-frame filtering and up to 2.54x lower end-to-end inference latency while improving benchmark accuracy. Canonical multimodal serving contribution.

title: Compiler-Grounded Hierarchical Diagnosis for LLM-Based Triton Kernel Optimization
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / NPU kernel optimization
why: Compiler-grounded hierarchical Triton-kernel diagnosis on Ascend NPU; 37-kernel benchmark reports 4.35x geometric-mean and 2.73x median speedup from initial to optimized kernels.

title: CONDUIT: A Unified Residual-Stream Restoration Framework for KV Cache Reuse in Vision-Language Models
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / KV cache reuse / visual-prefix reuse
why: CONDUIT is a training-free query-conditioned visual-token refresh policy for stale VLM KV reuse. At a 10% refresh budget it preserves 97.0-99.5% of full-prefill five-dataset average across three VLM backbones; on MMLongBench-Doc it uses 13.5% of full-prefill FLOPs and reports 2.99x TTFT speedup.

title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-context management
why: Tencent proactive context-management framework for long-horizon agents; planning, long-term memory and soft context offloading reduce working-context growth while improving long-context QA/deep-search performance. Official Tencent code/models are released.

title: Cost-Aware Hierarchical Multi-Agent Ransomware Detection and Family Attribution
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive multimodal routing / cost-aware orchestration
why: Uses confidence- and disagreement-aware hierarchical routing so cheap static analysis handles easy cases while dynamic, memory, and local-LLM verification are invoked selectively. It reports 43.97% lower average analysis cost than exhaustive analysis while retaining 96.57% binary accuracy and substantially reducing average latency except when the LLM fallback is used, providing measured agent-system efficiency evidence.

title: CREDIT: Cost-guided Reduction-reuse with Efficient DSMEM Inter-CTA Tiling
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / NVIDIA DSMEM / inter-CTA tiling
why: Direct GPU-kernel systems contribution accepted by HPEC 2026. Cost-guided DSMEM profitability model plus reduction-reuse transformation; beats torch.compile, Triton and optimized CUDA baselines on six workloads, with 1.466x geometric-mean speedup on RTX 5090 and 1.318x on H100; official source code is available.

title: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / computer-use agents / GUI+CLI runtime / trajectory efficiency
why: Builds a scalable environment-to-data pipeline for hybrid GUI+CLI computer-use agents and explicitly trains agents toward efficient hybrid paths. Its 9B model improves CUA-Verse by +39.3 score points while reducing steps 37% and tokens 60%; on OSWorld it improves success rate by 16.8 points while reducing steps 57% and tokens 44%. This is direct measured agent-runtime efficiency evidence rather than only an accuracy gain.

title: DAMP: Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision Recurrent-State Quantization
topic: quantization / recurrent-state memory / LLM inference
why: Direct inference-memory quantization for recurrent-state sequence models. Decay-aware mixed precision keeps sensitive channels high precision and reports 69.1% recurrent-state storage reduction, up to 2.01x recurrent-state update kernel speedup and up to 10.9% lower full-model TPOT.

title: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
topic: speculative decoding / diffusion language model acceleration
why: Training-free speculative decoding with diffusion-based tree drafts plus branch-conditioned AR correction; reports up to 12.97 accepted tokens per verification round and 9.73x lossless speedup over locally measured autoregressive decoding.

title: Deadline-Aware Adaptive Prefill Chunking for Efficient Large Language Model Serving
topic: LLM serving / chunked prefill / SLO scheduling / goodput
why: SLOWeave chooses the largest prefill chunk predicted to complete before the earliest active decode deadline. GPU-runtime evaluation reports 39% and 38% goodput gains over the strongest fixed-chunk baseline on mixed and long-context workloads at 25 ms TPOT, rising to 3.3x and 2.4x under a 10 ms objective.

title: Decoupled Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Talking Head Generation
topic: video/image generation acceleration / streaming diffusion / causal distillation
why: Decouples low-dimensional causal motion generation from a distilled causal diffusion renderer and runs both as parallel streams. Reports 15.4 FPS at 1.3 s latency with no quality degradation, directly addressing streaming generative inference efficiency.

title: Deformable Object Manipulation under Partial Observability via Real-Time Full-Shape Estimation
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot world model / real-time control
why: cRVAE replaces expensive online physics identification with a lightweight learned forward model from partial corner observations. It runs about 350x faster than XPBD on rope and over 1500x faster on fabric per forward pass, keeping receding-horizon planning within a 100 ms control budget and demonstrating hardware deployment on Unitree Go2.

title: DejaVu: Unifying Memory Allocations to Eliminate Redundant Copies on Unified-Memory SoCs
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / UMA / compiler-runtime memory optimization
why: DejaVu removes redundant CPU-GPU copies on unified-memory edge SoCs using a compile-time LLVM proof path and a profile-guided binary path for closed-source applications. Across seven benchmarks and three NVIDIA Jetson platforms, copy-dominated workloads speed up by up to 6.9x and closed-source end-to-end applications by 1.10-1.14x, reaching at least 99% of manual optimization performance.

title: DensityKV: Density-Guided KV Cache Compression for Long Video Generation
topic: KV cache / video generation acceleration / efficient attention
why: Training-free bounded historical KV-bank management for autoregressive video diffusion. Directly limits persistent historical KV growth while improving long-horizon consistency/stability at a fixed KV-capacity bound across three backbones.

title: Diamond Agent: Agentic Control of Federated HPC Resources as a Service
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / distributed training/inference / heterogeneous HPC orchestration
why: Agentic federated-HPC runtime with typed skills, cross-site resource discovery, Globus data movement, live queue-aware placement, and event-driven continuation. Across 27 hours of telemetry and 19 matched multi-site rounds (83 jobs) on four production supercomputers, it reduces median additional completion time relative to the fastest observed placement from 42 s to 4 s, a 10.5x reduction versus fixed-site placement.

title: Distill Globally, Adapt Locally: Reasoning Distillation and Product-Type Test-Time Training for Scalable Trade-Up Recommendation
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / distillation / scalable inference
why: Distills LLM reasoning into a 15.5M non-generative student that uses only two precomputed embeddings at inference. On a 100K-pair proxy catalog, the student on one eight-GPU machine is approximately 5,000x faster and 10,000x lower in estimated cost than direct LLM inference while retaining strong AUC, with lightweight product-type test-time adapters further improving AUC from 0.924 to 0.941.

title: Distilled Continuous Diffusion Language Models Can Write Code in Few Steps---or One
topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / diffusion language models / efficient reasoning
why: PlaidQ distills a continuous diffusion language model for code from hundreds of denoising steps to 16, a few, or even one step, shifting the quality-compute frontier; training/inference code and checkpoints are released by the authors.

title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
topic: distributed training/inference / GPU clusters / sparse optimization / communication
why: 24h primary scan recovered SHARDLP, a genuinely distributed GPU solver that keeps matrix and primal-dual state sharded end to end. Eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185B-variable/6.338B-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; support-aware communication cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. This is direct measured multi-GPU systems evidence.

title: DriftingVLA: Native One-Step Vision-Language-Action Generation via Per-Dimension Temporal Drifting
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / action-head acceleration
why: Protected Physical-AI direct inference acceleration: replaces iterative flow integration with native one-step action-chunk generation; reports 3.36x action-chunk generation speedup while retaining or improving task success.

title: DRLM: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based LLM Query Orchestration in Edge Environments
topic: edge/cloud heterogeneous AI systems / LLM serving / query orchestration / model-device-quantization routing
why: 30d edge/heterogeneous replay recovered a direct LLM serving orchestration paper absent from authority. DRLM combines class-conditioned quality and configuration-aware latency predictors with factorized PPO for state-aware model-device-quantization routing; a 64-node edge-cluster evaluation reports up to 51% inference-latency and 67% queuing-delay reduction with at most 8% accuracy loss.

title: DynaNDE: Dynamic Near-Data Expert Scheduling for Batched MoE Inference
topic: MoE systems / accelerators / heterogeneous inference
why: Dynamic NPU-NDP expert scheduling for batched MoE inference with hardware-heterogeneity and reuse-aware runtime; reports average 2.6x prefill and 2.2x decode speedup over prior NPU-NDP MoE serving.

title: Efficient Constant Optimization for Symbolic Regression with GPU-Accelerated Tree-Based Genetic Programming
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / GPU-resident batched optimization / CUDA / symbolic regression runtime
why: 7d lower-rank systematic replay recovered a GPU-resident optimization system absent from authority. The batched Levenberg-Marquardt solver uses a fixed number of population-wide CUDA launches per iteration and reverse-mode AD; on A100 it sustains up to 5.1e5 trees/s and at saturation delivers about 9.9x Operon throughput on a 64-core EPYC while matching fp64-reference quality.

title: Efficient On-Device Diffusion LLM Inference with Mobile NPU
topic: edge AI / diffusion LLM inference / mobile NPU / speculative decoding / KV reuse
why: 30d/90d-backup edge-cloud reverse census recovered llada.cpp, a direct NPU-aware dLLM inference framework absent from the authority. It combines multi-block speculative decoding, dual-path progressive revision, and a swap-optimized memory runtime; the primary paper reports 17-42x LLaDA-8B generation-latency reduction versus the CPU baseline with prefix KV reuse.

title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / active vision / adaptive compute
why: Digital foveation allocates high-resolution processing only around selected fixations. A single foveated observation preserves 95.9% of dense-baseline Top-1 and 96.9% Top-3 accuracy at only 4.7% of the computational cost; scene-level accumulation reaches 90.6% object recall at 58.6% compute. This is direct, measured adaptive-perception compute reduction with clear relevance to embodied and edge vision.

title: EFQ-Softmax: Exp-Free Quantization for Softmax
topic: quantization / efficient attention / low-bit inference kernels
why: EFQ-Softmax directly generates block-scaled E2M1 probability operands from shifted attention scores, removing the high-precision exp-then-quantize path while keeping FlashAttention-style normalization and accumulation. Evaluated on Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and WAN2.2-TI2V-5B, it preserves or improves quality and reduces fused probability-generation vector-stage latency by 40.33% on average for 16K-128K sequence lengths on the A5 vector unit.

title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / elastic inference / pruning / runtime adaptivity
why: SEC 2025 framework converts pretrained ViTs and CNNs into a single elastic family that switches operating modes at runtime rather than maintaining independent models. Experiments report up to 85% FLOP reduction, 50% latency reduction, and 76% memory-overhead reduction; official author repository is public.

title: Enabling High-Bandwidth Flash for Generative Recommendation Serving with Write-Aware KV Cache Policy
topic: LLM/recommendation serving / KV cache / flash tiering / endurance-aware cache policy
why: The work studies HBF-backed user-level KV reuse for generative recommendation and introduces admission-controlled write-aware LRU-K. Primary results report 3.8-4.7x throughput over HBM-only systems while extending modeled HBF lifetime from about one year to over six years at K=10 with comparable throughput.

title: Epoch: Compiling Diffusion Blocks for Sparse MoE Serving
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / diffusion language model serving / compiler-runtime
why: Epoch treats a diffusion-language-model block as a compilation unit, compiling active expert support and routing only live/new/refresh-required positions through fresh expert computation and expert-parallel communication. On 8 H100 GPUs across LLaDA-MoE variants from 7B to 100B, it improves end-to-end execution time by up to 2.7x over the strongest surviving baseline and remains feasible at batch sizes where baselines OOM while preserving quality.

title: EquiGQNet: Fast Grasp Quality Evaluation via Shared Equivariant Point Cloud Encoding
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / grasp planning / shared scene encoding
why: Encodes the point cloud once with SO(3)-equivariant features instead of rotating and re-encoding the scene for every grasp. CEM planning drops from 3.31 s to 0.48 s (6.9x speedup) while real-world decluttering reaches 95.2% grasp success and 230 picks/hour.

title: EStream: Fast and Memory-Efficient MoE Prefill through Expert Virtualization on Mobile NPUs
topic: edge AI systems / MoE serving / mobile NPU / expert virtualization
why: EStream runs dynamic MoE prefill entirely on a mobile NPU via one reusable expert graph and virtualizes expert weights from UFS through a bounded NPU-addressable arena. On a commercial Snapdragon smartphone across 18 settings it reports 2.25-27.57x pure-prefill TTFT speedup and 1.19-12.29x peak-memory reduction, scaling to 46.7B-parameter MoEs.

title: Every Kernel Is a Join: Automatic Multi-GPU Parallelism for AI Computations in Einsummable
topic: distributed training/inference / GPU systems / compiler
why: Automatically decomposes PyTorch-like AI computations across multi-GPU servers using join-aggregation specs and synthesized topology-aware exchange programs rather than canned collectives. On LLaMA blocks across eight A100 GPUs reports 8.97 ms geometric-mean runtime versus 13.80 ms hand-tuned PyTorch and 15.90 ms vLLM. Canonical systems/compiler work.

title: Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / post-training efficiency / sparse supervision
why: On-policy distillation experiments across Qwen3 and Llama configurations show that supervising only one or two generated tokens per reasoning trajectory, about 0.05% of all tokens, can match or surpass full-token supervision on reasoning while excluding the overwhelming majority of generated tokens from the training objective. The effect is reproduced across nine teacher-student configurations and GRPO/RLVR settings, making this unusually strong evidence for reasoning post-training efficiency.

title: Fast simulation of nonlinear deep resistive networks for energy-based computation
topic: AI accelerator / analog computing / simulator acceleration / energy-based computation
why: Extends coordinate-descent circuit simulation from ideal diodes to realistic monotone nonlinear devices. Across deep resistive networks it matches SPICE steady states with very low error while reaching speedups up to 1.7e3x; MNIST training on a 1568x100x20 double-Shockley network cuts per-epoch time by roughly 4.4e2x.

title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-action model inference / test-time video elimination
why: Direct inference-efficiency contribution: keeps video co-training but removes explicit future-video generation at test time. Reports 190 ms real-world latency and >4x speedup over imagine-then-execute WAMs while retaining competitive control performance.

title: FastE: Readout-Triggered Token Compression for LLM Embedding Inference
topic: LLM serving / embedding inference / token compression / retrieval systems
why: Training-free readout-triggered prefix compression for Qwen3-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Embedding. On NarrativeQA with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B it cuts decoder-backbone FLOPs by 40.11% while retaining 99.53% of full-forward nDCG@10, with configurable quality-efficiency trade-offs across text and cross-modal retrieval tasks.

title: Federated Binary Gating with Server-Side Vision-Language Inference for Surveillance Anomaly Classification
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge-cloud gating / selective VLM inference / federated systems
why: Uses a lightweight federated local video gate so only flagged clips invoke server-side Qwen3-VL-8B. In a real three-node heterogeneous deployment, fixed-threshold routing preserves nearly the same macro-F1 as centralized CNN+VLM while transmitting only 51.4% of videos, providing measured selective-offload and server-VLM utilization reduction.

title: FedSubMuon: Communication-Efficient Federated LLM Fine-Tuning via Structured Subspace Muon
topic: distributed training/inference / federated LLM fine-tuning / communication efficiency
why: Optimizes compact coefficient matrices inside shared structured subspaces so clients avoid transmitting full layer-sized Muon updates. Across matched communication budgets FedSubMuon performs best; on Dolly-15K the closest communication baseline requires 5.5x and 1.4x more total communication for Llama-1B and Qwen-4B. This is direct measured LLM communication-efficiency evidence.

title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?
topic: KV cache/long-context / RAG serving / prefill acceleration
why: Combines KV-concatenation-aware fine-tuning with selective KV recomputation for long-context RAG. On RULER at 124k tokens it improves score by 9.7 points over recompute-only while reducing TTFT by 80% versus full attention, directly addressing the quality-efficiency tradeoff in reusable KV caches.

title: FleetOpt: Analytical Fleet Provisioning for LLM Inference with Compress-and-Route as Implementation Mechanism
topic: LLM serving / heterogeneous GPU fleet / context-length routing / fleet provisioning
why: Junchen Jiang reverse census recovered a direct LLM fleet-provisioning framework absent from the current authority. FleetOpt analytically derives a two-pool context-length topology and uses Compress-and-Route as the implementation mechanism; on production traces it reports 6-82% total GPU-cost reduction versus a homogeneous fleet.

title: FlexSpIM: An Event-Based Digital Compute-In-Memory Accelerator with Flexible Operand Resolution and Layer-Wise Hybrid Stationarity
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / SNN accelerator / digital CIM
why: FlexSpIM is a fabricated 40-nm digital compute-in-memory SNN accelerator with bitwise operand-resolution reconfiguration and hybrid layer-wise stationarity. Prototype/system evaluation reports up to 45% energy and 52% latency reduction versus fixed-stationarity approaches while retaining 95.8% DVS gesture accuracy.

title: FlowPrefill: Decoupling Preemption from Prefill Scheduling Granularity to Mitigate Head-of-Line Blocking in LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / prefill scheduling / operator-level preemption / SLO goodput
why: Direct LLM-serving systems work that decouples preemption granularity from scheduling frequency via operator-level preemption and event-driven scheduling; reports up to 5.6x maximum goodput while satisfying heterogeneous SLOs on production traces.

title: Following a Unique Path: A Fast Certifier Applied to Outlier-Robust Pose Registration
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robotic perception / optimization runtime
why: CP-Cert exploits indirect linear algebra, sparsity and parallelism to certify degenerate pose-registration relaxations efficiently. It reaches runtimes up to three orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art direct solvers and is integrated into an outlier-robust real-world pose-estimation pipeline.

title: ForgeStencil: Automating Per-Case Stencil Specialization from Kernels to 100+ Real Applications
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / code-generation agents / CUDA specialization
why: ForgeStencil uses code-synthesis agents to generate per-case CUDA kernels and end-to-end application rewrites, with a measurement-integrity harness rejecting invalid gains. Same-precision f32 kernels reach 2.35x geometric-mean speedup over per-case SOTA baselines on A100, and end-to-end application median speedup is 1.41x across 100 real codes.

title: Forgetting Without Restarting: Execution-State Unlearning for Stateful LLM Agents
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / stateful agent runtime / KV cache / selective replay
why: 30d agent-runtime replay recovered a systems mechanism absent from authority. It formalizes execution-state unlearning across prompt, compressed memory, pending state and KV cache, and implements provenance-guided selective replay: locate the revoked information injection point, crop/restore the KV checkpoint, and regenerate only the tainted suffix instead of restarting the entire trajectory. The paper reports counterfactual-equivalent behavior with up to 9x fewer recomputed tokens than full reset.

title: Foundry: Template-Based CUDA Graph Context Materialization for Fast LLM Serving Cold Start
topic: LLM serving / CUDA graph / cold-start / autoscaling
why: Template-based CUDA graph topology+execution-context materialization for dynamic LLM serving. Across dense and MoE models up to 235B, reports up to 99% cold-start reduction; Qwen3-235B-A22B initialization drops from about 10 minutes to 3.9 seconds while retaining CUDA-graph throughput.

title: FPGA Acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption with Adaptive Key Switching
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / FPGA acceleration
why: Co-designs a memory-efficient KLSS datapath with a runtime selector between HKS and KLSS and eliminates off-chip ciphertext transfers. On Alveo U280 it achieves 1.84-3.31x bootstrapping speedup and 1.66-2.52x secure image-classification speedup over state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators, providing strong measured accelerator evidence.

title: FrankenReport: Early Exiting in Long-Form Generation Using Expected Value of Computation
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive computation / early exit / deep research serving
why: Introduces section-level expected-value-of-computation gating so long-form research generation can stop targeted computation when predicted quality gains are small. In simulation it outperforms random allocation by up to 4x under low budgets and smoothly recovers full-pipeline quality as budget increases, providing direct adaptive-compute evidence for agentic/deep-research workloads.

title: From 80x to 385x: A Best-Matching-Unit Search at the L2 Roof, Measured Against a Symmetrically Tuned Baseline
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / memory-bandwidth optimization / sparse search
why: This work symmetrically tunes both SparseBin and cuSPARSE baselines for SOM best-matching-unit search, using tiling, membership clustering, neuron-axis chunking and vectorized loads. The tuned kernel reaches 5.6-10.1x per-epoch improvement over the prior configuration and about 385x over the earlier CUDA implementation while reaching 77% of peak L2 bandwidth, making it a direct measured GPU-kernel optimization result.

title: From Monolithic Blending to Agentic Orchestration: Dynamic Response for Conversational Assistants at Scale
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / production conversational serving / orchestration / GPU footprint
why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a production-scale agent-serving system absent from authority. The migration replaces a monolithic 235B blended responder with a bounded ReAct orchestrator plus smaller generator; serving optimizations reduce orchestrator P90 latency from 3.87 s to 2.24 s, reduce GPU footprint by roughly one-third, and cut estimated annual serving cost by more than an order of magnitude. Accepted to EMNLP 2026 Industry Track.

title: GaLe: memory-efficient Global Approximate and Local Exact features
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / memory-efficient inference
why: GaLe enables pretrained hybrid CNN-transformer inference on constrained devices without retraining by combining local exact and global approximate features; on Cortex-M33 it reports up to 65% speedup and 90% RAM reduction versus patch-based inference while matching exact-inference performance.

title: GaussianDream++: Efficient 3D Gaussian World Modeling for Robotic Manipulation
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / efficient 3D world modeling
why: Physical-AI protected canonical: distills training-time current/future 3D Gaussian supervision into 20 policy-native world tokens; removes renderer, Gaussian decoder and heavy VGGT/TGE pathway at inference, avoiding online Gaussian rollout while preserving efficient closed-loop control.

title: GloVLA: Let Geometry Move and Local VLA Interact for Robust Object-Centric Manipulation in Unstructured Environments
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hybrid control / inference reduction
why: GloVLA separates global geometric transport from short-horizon local VLA interaction. On physical UR10e tasks it raises success from 35.6% to 90.0% while more than halving mean VLA inference time, directly reducing expensive VLA invocation along the trajectory.

title: GPU-Accelerated Gate-Level Time-Based Power Analysis via Event-Density-Aware Partitioning and Kernel Fusion
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / EDA acceleration / kernel fusion / workload partitioning
why: First GPU-accelerated gate-level time-based power analysis framework, combining state-dependent power retrieval, event-density-aware GPU thread partitioning, and fused power-computation kernels. The primary abstract reports up to 37.63x end-to-end speedup over multi-threaded Synopsys PrimeTime PX while maintaining high accuracy.

title: GPU-Accelerated Hypergraph Partitioning and Placement to Map SNNs on Neuromorphic Hardware
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / neuromorphic accelerator / GPU compiler-mapping
why: This work builds a GPU-accelerated hypergraph partitioning and placement pipeline for mapping million-neuron SNNs to neuromorphic cores. The mapper is 18-280x faster on average than sequential tools while model-based evaluation reports up to 16% lower communication latency and 42% lower spike-movement energy.

title: GPU-Enabled Large-Scale Optimization Using Randomized Linear Algebra
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / scientific ML / randomized linear algebra
why: rlaopt is an Apache-licensed PyTorch package that exposes GPU-enabled randomized-linear-algebra solvers for positive-definite systems and constrained convex empirical-risk problems, including NystromPCG, NysADMM and SAPPHIRE. The primary abstract reports substantial GPU-execution speedups across ridge regression, bounded multinomial logistic regression and bounded elastic net, while also supporting differentiation through solver iterations, making this a practical reusable GPU systems/runtime contribution.

title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / JAX / differentiable scientific computing
why: GRADSOLVE is an open-source JAX GPU runtime for exact discrete-adjoint gradients of low-dimensional ODE ensembles. The primary abstract reports a 2.8x forward-solver speedup over DiffEqGPU.jl and 5.6-14.1x faster gradient computation than Diffrax checkpointed adjoints at matched forward-state accuracy across three GPU generations, providing direct measured GPU-kernel/runtime evidence.

title: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / asynchronous LLM agents / GUI testing / cost-aware tool use
why: Uses history-aware cluster memory, asynchronous intent generation, and hybrid fulfillment that reserves the LLM for complex intents while routing simple intents to a lightweight heuristic. Across 41 Android apps it achieves up to 36.4% higher code coverage while costing less than one eighth of the best pure-LLM baseline, directly addressing LLM-agent latency and cost.

title: Grid Games: The Power of Multiple Grids for Quantizing Large Language Models
topic: LLM quantization; microscaled FP4; adaptive grids; hardware data formats
why: ISTA DASLab canonical miss: adaptive per-block grid selection improves microscaled FP4 quantization and introduces hardware-oriented SFP4-style grid families with TensorCore implementability.

title: GrowPage: On-Demand KV Budgeting for Efficient LLM Reasoning Serving
topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning / LLM serving
why: Treats KV capacity itself as a runtime resource and acquires physical pages on demand from evolving attention working sets while preserving PagedAttention continuous batching and prefix caching; reports superior performance-throughput trade-off across reasoning workloads. Canonical systems contribution.

title: GSQ: Highly-Accurate Low-Precision Scalar Quantization for LLMs via Gumbel-Softmax Sampling
topic: LLM quantization / 1-3 bit scalar PTQ / kernel-compatible deployment / MoE compression
why: DASLab reverse-census recall miss: Gumbel-Softmax scalar PTQ closes much of the 2-3 bit gap to vector/trellis methods while retaining standard scalar formats; scales to trillion-parameter MoE and is compatible with optimized integer/GGUF deployment kernels.

title: Gutenberg: Taming Latency-Critical Cloud Services with Near-Data-Processing
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / near-data processing / latency-critical cloud services / tail latency
why: 7d full-PASS lower-rank replay recovered a direct systems paper on mutable latency-critical cloud services. Gutenberg jointly controls page placement, replication, CPU/NDP execution and routing, using delta-buffered writable replication and CPU helpers; on TailBench with ZSim/Ramulator-calibrated timing it reports average and p99 latency reductions up to 80.4% and 85.8% versus prior systems while improving isolation and fairness.

title: H3DNAS: Hardware-Aware ONNX-Native 3D Point Cloud Model Compression
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / sparsity-pruning / deployment compiler
why: H3DNAS performs hardware-aware compression directly on ONNX graphs without original source or gradients, using a channel dependency graph, hierarchical search and graph surgery. On Jetson Orin Nano-class deployment targets it reduces parameters by 43.2-65.5% and achieves 1.29-1.99x inference speedups with negligible accuracy loss.

title: Hardware-Accelerated Instance Segmentation for Resource-Constrained Space Robotics with Criticality Analysis
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge accelerator / quantization / reliable robotics inference
why: Deployment-oriented Physical-AI systems paper combining quantization calibration, DPU architectural adaptation to reduce CPU fallback, bounded-latency execution, and radiation criticality analysis on a lunar micro-rover. Reports 309 ms inference at 5.7 W, recovers 69.8% of quantization-induced accuracy loss, and targeted mitigation lowers global criticality by 31.7%.

title: HBF Sucks? A Full-Stack Characterization of High-Bandwidth Flash for KV-Centric LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / heterogeneous memory and storage
why: Full-stack characterization of high-bandwidth flash for KV-centric LLM serving using four two-hour Qwen-Bailian production traces, five dense/MoE models, and H100/B200 profiles. Shows a drop-in HBF-for-SSD design can worsen end-to-end latency by 2-5.5x and SLO goodput by 1.1-2.7x because near-tier capacity/bandwidth loss, write-heavy transient KV traffic, thermal limits, and endurance dominate raw flash read latency; establishes concrete system-design conditions for selective HBF placement.

title: HBFSim: Fast and Faithful Simulation of High-Bandwidth Flash Under Real GPU Execution
topic: LLM serving / GPU memory hierarchy / simulation / HBF
why: First evaluation platform applying High-Bandwidth-Flash timing, capacity, and thermal effects while a real LLM workload executes on real GPU kernels, using PTX rewriting and launch gating. It preserves unmodified vLLM/Qwen3-30B-A3B token outputs, matches all six device calibration breakpoints, and its device fast path runs the evaluated case in 2s versus 44s for the detailed reference path (20.8x), enabling practical pre-silicon memory-tier studies.

title: HDA-MoE: Hybrid Parallelism and Dynamic, Adaptive Scheduling for Mixture-of-Experts with 3D Near-Memory Processing
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / 3D near-memory processing / hybrid parallelism / runtime scheduling
why: HDA-MoE co-designs offline hybrid TP/EP mapping and online adaptive scheduling for MoE inference on 3D near-memory processing. The primary arXiv abstract reports 1.1-3.4x speedup over TP, 1.1-1.5x over EP, 1.1-3.7x over a hybrid compute-balanced baseline, and 1.1-1.3x over HD-MoE, with source code released.

title: HEAT: Faster Fully Homomorphic Inference via Approximations-Weights Co-Adaptation
topic: LLM serving / privacy-preserving inference / FHE acceleration
why: HEAT makes per-nonlinearity approximation iteration counts learnable and co-adapts them with model weights. On encrypted GPT-2 decoding it reports 3.1x fewer iterations, 1.6x fewer bootstraps and 1.4x lower end-to-end latency while improving decode agreement.

title: Heterogeneous Memory Design Exploration for AI Accelerators with a Gain Cell Memory Compiler
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems; AI accelerator memory; SRAM/GCRAM; compiler; hardware design-space exploration
why: Stanford Thierry Tambe hardware-memory canonical gap: OpenGCRAM compiler jointly explores SRAM and gain-cell RAM macro designs, enabling heterogeneous on-chip memory choices for AI accelerators under area, delay and power objectives.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The Overlooked Significance of Canonical Elements for Extreme LLM Sparsity
topic: sparsity/pruning / LLM inference / decoding acceleration / memory efficiency
why: 7d full-PASS lower-rank replay recovered a directly measured extreme-sparsity LLM inference result. Progressive second-order sparsification plus continued training preserves useful quality to 95-99% sparsity; on LLaMA-2-7B the paper reports 3.23x decoding speedup and 6.21x memory savings at 95% sparsity, making it directly relevant to efficient inference rather than only model compression.

title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding
topic: KV cache compression; LLM decoding; algorithm-hardware co-design; long context
why: Fresh KU Leuven MICAS/Marian Verhelst neighborhood recheck surfaced an uncatalogued algorithm-hardware KV-cache paper. HiKV performs hierarchical token- and element-level importance-aware compression and couples it with dedicated hardware support for efficient LLM decoding.

title: HiRAD: A Flexible Large-Scale AGV Routing System
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / real-time multi-agent routing / hierarchical RL / edge control
why: Uses hierarchical heading/velocity control and an asynchronous event-driven decision pipeline to reduce inference complexity from O(n^2) to O(n). It cuts per-step decision latency by up to 71% and reduces makespan by 45-63% on large AGV routing workloads, directly satisfying real-time Physical-AI runtime efficiency criteria.

title: HoneyRoute: Honeypot-Model Routing for Adversarial LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / routing / security-aware inference
why: HoneyRoute adds a lightweight serving router that diverts malicious requests to a honeypot model. It achieves F1=.911 with 38 ms median added latency, approximately 1/385 the latency of a two-tier guard-LLM cascade, while reducing production-model token consumption by 97.8% under adversarial flooding.

title: How to Speculate about Uncertainty in Agentic Coding? A Draft-Model Gate Method
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / speculative methods / runtime gating / token cost
why: Uses a small open-weight draft model to score already-generated black-box agent trajectories in one forward pass and gate risky actions before execution. On Qwen3-Coder-480B and Claude 3.5 Sonnet software agents it reduces execution error by 6-8 percentage points and deployment token cost by 14-19%, including out-of-distribution transfer without retraining.

title: HybridFLow: SDN-Orchestrated Client Partitioning for Hybrid Federated Learning
topic: distributed training / edge-cloud / federated learning / network-aware scheduling
why: Closed-loop SDN orchestration estimates per-client communication time and partitions synchronous versus asynchronous FL clients using network-wide bottleneck visibility. Across multiple topologies it reaches 80% target accuracy 33-40% faster than SmartFLow and cuts average round duration by 30-40 seconds.

title: HyQuant: Hybrid-Precision Quantization for LLM Attention
topic: quantization / KV cache / efficient attention
why: Hybrid-precision attention quantization preserves selected vertical-line and local-window states while quantizing most context; decode path fuses KV dequantization with attention, directly targeting attention/KV memory and hardware efficiency.

title: InstantMimic: A High Performance System for Learning Physics-based Skills in Seconds
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / GPU systems / robotics training
why: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 system that removes fragmented-kernel and CPU-memory bottlenecks by making simulation, environment computation, policy inference, and policy updates one GPU-native execution flow. The resulting end-to-end pipeline trains diverse physics-based imitation skills in seconds and makes LLM-agent hyperparameter search practical; directly relevant to efficient Physical-AI training/runtime systems.

title: Interface-Aware KV Cache Quantization for Dense On-Chip NVM in Long-Context LLM Decoding
topic: KV cache/long-context / quantization / NVM / accelerator co-design
why: This work co-designs 4-bit KV quantization with dense on-chip NVM and fixed-range converters rather than assuming GPU-style metadata. Across 3B-14B models and contexts to 32K, it maintains accuracy under modeled device noise while reporting 3.1-3.6x lower KV read energy than KIVI/KVQuant mapped to the same NVM and about 8x lower metadata overhead than KIVI.

title: Intra-Prompt Parallel Decoding for Common-Context Question Answering
topic: LLM serving / parallel decoding / shared-context inference
why: IPPD answers multiple questions sharing one context inside a single prompt using virtual position IDs and attention-mask manipulation, requiring no fine-tuning or architecture change. It reports up to 7x effective throughput over standard decoding without quality degradation and outperforms prefix caching with PagedAttention in most settings; accepted to EMNLP 2026 main.

title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
topic: GPU kernel / DSL / compiler; TPU/Pallas autonomous kernel optimization
why: Google/TPU kernel-systems canonical gap: introduces a 50-workload TPU-native benchmark for autonomous Pallas kernel optimization, with production LLM operators and hand-tuned Tokamax references; reports documentation-conditioned agents solving 48/50 workloads at 1.28x geomean and Autocomp at 1.36x over XLA.

title: Jetson-PI: Towards Onboard Real-Time Robot Control via Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Inference
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge deployment / asynchronous inference / scheduling / runtime
why: Jetson-PI targets onboard real-time VLA inference on Jetson-class edge devices. It combines a lightweight foresight-aligned future-correction module, confidence-based VLM/action-expert scheduling, CUDA graph reuse, GPU-resident buffering and flow unrolling. The paper reports 8.66x and 5.41x higher control frequency than naive PyTorch and vla.cpp on Jetson Orin, while improving average LIBERO success rate over VLASH by 14.8%.

title: Jina-OCR-v1: Efficient Document Parsing with Speculative Decoding and Dense Verifiable Rewards
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / speculative decoding / efficient OCR
why: Deployment-oriented multimodal model explicitly built for low-budget GPUs. FastMTP recursively reuses one draft block for K=3 speculative steps with lossless greedy verification; on NVIDIA L4 it doubles decode speed and reaches 2.57 pages/s. Official model is public.

title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
topic: agentic LLM serving; power efficiency; context-aware GPU DVFS; memory-aware scheduling; multi-instance routing
why: Fresh major-group saturation recheck of the Michigan SymbioticLab/Mosharaf Chowdhury lineage surfaced a true paper-level miss. KAIROS treats evolving agent context as a first-class control signal and jointly manages GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance placement; it reports 27% average and up to 39.8% GPU power reduction while meeting performance targets on agentic workloads.

title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory / agent runtime / context management
why: AIOS kernel-managed shared memory centralizes retrieval, privacy enforcement, and prompt injection across agents. Across GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B in 1,800 trials, it approaches full-context personalization while using much shorter prompts and reduces end-to-end latency by 15-61%, with corresponding token and inference-cost reductions.

title: Knowing When to Stop: Adaptive Action Chunking via Internal Cross-Attention Dynamics in VLAs
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive action execution
why: Training-free adaptive VLA action-chunk truncation using already-computed cross-attention entropy; directly targets the inference-frequency versus open-loop accuracy tradeoff with negligible additional overhead on pi0.5 and X-VLA across simulation and real manipulation.

title: KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU
topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory virtualization
why: Direct KV-context virtualization system spanning GPU, host memory and NVMe with attention-space indexing. Demonstrates 1M-token agent workspaces on a 24GB RTX 5090 Laptop GPU, roughly 50 tokens/s local generation, and improved task success over compaction-only baselines.

title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
topic: efficient attention / KV cache / long-context inference / serving runtime
why: Introduces Declarative Attention: the model declares global/focus/local attention spans and the inference engine skips irrelevant KV-cache reads. Across 15 long-context tasks it reduces attended decode tokens by 52.0% and 31.1% on two off-the-shelf models; includes a vLLM-compatible block-masking runtime path.

title: Lantern: Finding Committable Transactions via Back-Propagation on DAGs
topic: distributed training/inference / data systems / transaction runtime
why: Deterministic concurrency control without prior read-write sets. Lantern uses DAG back-propagation to identify additional committable transactions and conflict-free batch selection for read-modify-write workloads. Integrated into ChainMaker and evaluated on YCSB and SmallBank, it reaches up to 4.2x throughput over Aria and at least 2.2x execution-layer throughput improvement, providing direct measured systems evidence.

title: Laplacian Frequency Hierarchies for Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting Training
topic: video/image generation acceleration / 3D Gaussian Splatting / efficient training
why: Frequency-staged 3DGS training archives lower-frequency Gaussian fields so later stages optimize residuals with fewer active primitives. The primary abstract reports average training speedups of 1.73x/1.21x at 1K and 1.74x/1.33x at 4K when combined with Taming-3DGS/FastGS, with competitive reconstruction quality.

title: Latency-Aware Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows on Heterogeneous GPUs
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / heterogeneous GPU serving
why: Prediction-guided runtime constructs physical execution graphs for concurrent multi-agent workflows on heterogeneous GPU pools, jointly optimizing model lifecycle, fusion, placement and execution order; reports up to 36.8% makespan and 25.9% p95 completion-latency reduction. Canonical agent-serving systems work.

title: LatentPress: Context Compression Beyond Text and Vision
topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / context compression
why: LatentPress compresses long conversational/document context into continuous memory tokens read directly by a frozen decoder. It reports 4-16x compression, about 43 ms write latency, and 5-9x faster compressed-prefix reading than raw context or cached OCR while matching or exceeding raw-context QA in several regimes.

title: LeanGRPO: Eliminating Redundant Recomputation in Diffusion RL
topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / efficient training / reasoning post-training
why: Eliminates mathematically redundant selected-timestep recomputation in diffusion RL through retain/reweight recompute-free schedules, preserving the original objective and reporting up to 1.83x end-to-end speedup on FLUX.1-dev and Wan. Canonical efficient post-training contribution.

title: Learning Agent Execution for KV-Cache Management in Agentic Serving
topic: LLM serving / agent systems / KV cache / cache eviction / prefetching
why: CacheScout is a direct AI-infra runtime contribution for multi-agent LLM serving. It learns agent execution transitions online and uses them for KV-cache eviction and proactive prefetching on top of vLLM, reporting 10-18 percentage-point higher cache hit rate, 18-45% lower mean TTFT, 29-38% lower per-turn latency, and up to 57% higher peak throughput.

title: Lightweight Vision Transformer Compression for On-Device Plant Disease Detection in Resource-Constrained Agricultural Field Conditions
topic: quantization / sparsity-pruning / edge AI deployment
why: Unified H-BAC pruning, quantization and distillation pipeline for on-device ViT deployment. Primary results retain 95.13% baseline accuracy while reducing model size by 74-98%; the fully integrated configuration compresses 327.42 MB to 6.01 MB, a 54.5x size reduction, with 95.13 +/- 2.32% accuracy. The paper also fairly reports that a directly trained same-size student can be competitive, making the deployment trade-off especially useful.

title: LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
topic: LLM serving / RAG / retrieval efficiency / context reduction
why: Replaces retrieval-time LLM control with query-conditioned graph exploration and reasoning-chain context construction. On DistComp it cuts per-query latency by over 100x and cost by over 99% versus GraphRAG Global and DRIFT while achieving the best reported overall quality; on UltraDomain it matches LinearRAG quality with about 14x fewer tokens. This is direct measured RAG serving efficiency evidence.

title: LiveVVT: High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-On in Real Time
topic: video generation acceleration / streaming diffusion / rolling recurrent generation / few-step distillation
why: 30d video-generation acceleration replay recovered a direct real-time diffusion serving mechanism absent from authority. LiveVVT converts complete-clip bidirectional diffusion into rolling bounded-lookahead streaming generation, adds bounded temporal plus persistent appearance memories, and progressively distills to few-step recurrent inference. It reports 26x lower latency and 11x higher throughput while preserving high-fidelity long-sequence generation.

title: Llamas on the Web: Memory-Efficient, Performance-Portable, and Multi-Precision LLM Inference with WebGPU
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM inference / WebGPU / multi-precision / browser runtime
why: Microsoft Research LlamaWeb is a direct inference-runtime contribution: a WebGPU backend for llama.cpp with static memory planning, tunable kernels and multi-precision support. Evaluated on 16 devices from 8 vendors, it reports 29-33% lower memory than browser baselines and 45-69% higher decode throughput across four GPUs, making it a strong heterogeneous/on-device AI systems paper.

title: Loom: Weaving Diagnostic Strands into Free-Text Consensus via Embedding-Space Reweighting
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / inference latency / consensus
why: Loom replaces deep monolithic RCA agents with deterministic embedding-space consensus plus one lightweight LLM synthesis call. On OpenRCA it occupies the accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier while running about 26x faster than a state-of-the-art autonomous agent, or about 33x with an 8B synthesizer.

title: LoSA: Near-Lossless Sparse Attention for Training-Free Video Diffusion Acceleration
topic: video/image generation acceleration / sparse attention / video diffusion
why: Direct video diffusion inference acceleration. Retains 99% attention mass with reusable block-sparse patterns; reports 1.36x standalone speedup and up to 3.2x when composed with feature caching with near-lossless VBench quality.

title: LPM: Industrial-Scale Generative Video Restoration
topic: video/image generation acceleration; diffusion serving; industrial video restoration; quantization; TensorRT-LLM
why: Kuaishou production video-system canonical gap: training-aware consistency distillation plus FP8 DiT, SageAttention, INT8 tiled VAE, TensorRT-LLM, operator fusion and custom CUDA kernels yield 39.5x end-to-end speedup over the original 25-step pipeline; deployed at industrial scale on content accounting for about 45% of Kuaishou viewing time.

title: LUMIN: Lightweight Universal Manufacturing Inspection Network for Anomaly Detection
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient inference / memory bank
why: LUMIN targets both memory-bank construction and inference. PSP makes sampling 341x faster than FPS, while parallel similarity computation reduces inference memory and latency by over 95% and stratified evaluation reduces computation time by 20x with negligible metric loss.

title: LycheeDecode: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Hybrid-Head Sparse Decoding
topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient attention / LLM decoding
why: Direct long-context inference acceleration with a hardware-efficient top-k hybrid-head sparse decoding mechanism, reporting up to 2.7x speedup at 128K context while preserving quality. It fills a canonical long-context/efficient-attention neighborhood absent from authority.

title: Lynx: Progressive Speculative Quantization for accelerating KV Transfer in Long-Context Inference
topic: LLM serving / disaggregated inference / KV cache transfer / progressive quantization / speculative decoding
why: Direct AI-infra systems work for disaggregated long-context inference. Splits KV into high-priority Anchor bits and Residual bits, begins speculative decode after Anchor arrival while Residual transfer overlaps, then verifies against higher precision. Reports up to 1.43x TTFT improvement over INT8 while matching BF16-level accuracy.

title: MatGPTQ: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Matryoshka Quantization
topic: LLM quantization; Matryoshka precision; PTQ; mixed-precision kernels
why: ISTA DASLab canonical miss: one-shot PTQ produces a single sliceable multi-precision model, adds budget-aware heterogeneous bit allocation and efficient mixed-precision execution kernels.

title: Matrix-Game 3.5: Enhancing Real-Time Streaming Interactive World Models with Patch Memory
topic: Physical AI / interactive world model / streaming video generation / patch memory / real-time distillation
why: Protected Physical-AI/world-model replay recovered an efficient interactive-world-model paper absent from authority. Matrix-Game 3.5 combines geometry-aware patch memory and tiled projective RoPE with static/dynamic world representation, then uses progressive real-time distillation to turn a bidirectional diffusion model into a few-step causal generator for minute-long real-time interactive generation. This is directly relevant to WAM serving/runtime and long-horizon state reuse.

title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
topic: LLM serving / private inference / verifiable delegation / heterogeneous offload
why: End-to-end Qwen3-4B prototype delegates dominant matrix-vector products while preserving input privacy and verifiability with virtually no server verification overhead. With one client thread, throughput improves up to 17x with online privacy masks, 45x with precomputed masks, and 44x for verification-only; client-side microbenchmarks with simulated network delay reach 12-157x depending on mode.

title: MaxKernel: Agentic Kernel Generation for TPUs
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / TPU kernel generation / agentic optimization
why: Direct kernel/infra contribution. Multi-agent TPU kernel engineering system with compiler feedback, testing, profiling and autotuning; evaluated on 50 JaxBench tasks plus real open-source workloads, matching expert hand-tuned baselines, with official open-source implementation.

title: MeanField Surrogate Modeling for Scalable Runtime Scheduling of Concurrent Heterogeneous AI Inference on Shared GPUs
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / GPU scheduling / concurrent inference
why: Direct runtime-scheduling systems paper, accepted by IEEE Embedded Systems Letters. MeanField surrogate models concurrent LLM+vision inference with approximately linear profiling growth; scheduler handles 78,732 feasible N=5 configurations, stays within 0.10% of exhaustive search with zero SLA violations, and makes decisions at 26 ms median, about 5x faster than exhaustive surrogate search.

title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / RAG agents / model compression / deployment selection
why: Deployment-centered edge AI contribution that selects a structurally compressed sub-network per device using measured on-device throughput, judged RAG quality, a general-capability floor, and memory budget. A weight-shared supernetwork makes selection practical; case study spans three heterogeneous edge tiers at 1.3-5 W standby.

title: MedFlow: Class-Aware Multi-Scale Generation for Medical Time-Series Synthesis
topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / generative inference / sampling throughput / time-series
why: 7d replay recovered a flow-matching generation system with direct measured sampling efficiency. Across four medical time-series datasets it reports 3.8x higher sampling throughput while also improving downstream utility and Context-FID, making it relevant to diffusion/flow inference efficiency despite the application domain.

title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory compression / retrieval
why: MemForest compresses continuously accumulated agent memory with event-centric partitioning, EventTree progressive merging, and anchor-guided retrieval. At 50% compression it retains 97.1% of Mem0 performance with 1.89x retrieval speedup, and 99.7% of M3-Agent performance with 2.24x retrieval speedup across robot/web multimodal benchmarks.

title: MemoryLACE: Memory Lifecycle-Aware Consolidation and Evidence Retrieval
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term agent memory / runtime efficiency
why: Lifecycle-aware sparse merge/supersession/contradiction memory for long-term LLM agents. On BEAM it reports 66.6% lower end-to-end runtime than Hindsight while improving same-backbone quality, making it a direct agent-memory runtime result rather than only a memory-quality method.

title: MINERVA: How Small Can a Manipulation Policy Be and Still Solve LIBERO?
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / compact policy / deployment efficiency
why: Empirically estimates LIBERO task-capacity floor: a 0.54M-parameter policy reaches 95.1% average success over 2,000 rollouts, runs 5-9 ms per action chunk on laptop CPU, and exposes weak robustness/task-ID memorization in standard LIBERO. Strong deployment-efficiency and benchmark-diagnostic result; protected Physical-AI canonical-high.

title: MINT: A Unified Model for World-Space Camera and Hand Motion Estimation from Scalable Egocentric Pipeline Supervision
