topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / egocentric perception / unified inference
why: MINT replaces a multi-stage camera/depth/hand trajectory pipeline with one shared spatiotemporal model and explicit coordinate transforms. It approaches state of the art on public benchmarks while achieving a 3.67x end-to-end speedup over the labeling pipeline that supervises it.

title: Mix-Quant: Quantized Prefilling, Precise Decoding for Agentic LLMs
topic: agentic LLM inference; quantized prefill; NVFP4; prefill-decode disaggregation
why: NUS xML canonical miss: phase-aware agent serving quantizes compute-heavy prefilling to NVFP4 while preserving BF16 decoding; reports up to 3x prefill speedup and provides a modified-vLLM disaggregated serving pipeline.

title: mjorbit: A Simulation Framework for Space Robotics
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robotics runtime / GPU simulation
why: mjorbit extends MuJoCo with spacecraft dynamics, actuators and sensors and exposes both low-latency C++ CPU and high-throughput GPU backends for contact-rich space robotics. It demonstrates realistic on-orbit MPC and RL case studies and provides open-source code, making it a concrete Physical-AI runtime/simulation infrastructure contribution.

title: Modality-Decoupled Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Embodied Intelligence in 6G
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / distributed training / edge-cloud / communication compression
why: IEEE Wireless Communications accepted FedMVLA decouples vision, language, and action updates for federated embodied intelligence. A 3GPP-based robotic-manipulation case study reaches 84.8% success, +22.2 points over FedAvg, scales to 128 clients across eight cells, and cuts schedule-averaged per-client uplink model-update payload by 95.6% while keeping p95 round-critical uplink completion near 1.5 s.

title: Model Compression with Exact Budget Constraints via Riemannian Manifolds
topic: LLM compression; mixed-precision quantization; MoE expert pruning; exact-budget optimization
why: ISTA DASLab true canonical miss found on fresh recheck: RCO optimizes the actual loss under an exact compression budget using Riemannian constrained optimization, covering mixed-precision quantization and MoE expert pruning with exact feasibility and lower search cost.

title: MolParser-Mobile: Ultrafast OCSR System for Large-Scale Chemical Literature Mining
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient vision inference / high-throughput deployment / lightweight model systems
why: 7d lower-rank replay recovered a deployment-oriented vision inference system whose bottleneck is explicitly throughput. MolParser-Mobile uses an AutoML-optimized lightweight end-to-end OCSR architecture with 9.98M parameters and reports 1,520 molecules/s on a single RTX 4090D while maintaining competitive recognition accuracy, making the measured inference-efficiency contribution strong enough for canonical retention.

title: Multi-Turn LLM Conversations under the Least-Recently-Used Policy: Mean-Field Asymptotics and Hit Ratio Approximation
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / multi-turn conversations / cache provisioning
why: Direct LLM-serving/KV systems contribution. Derives a mean-field closed-form limit and practical LRU KV-cache hit-ratio estimator for growing multi-turn prefixes, then validates the estimator with real Qwen3-8B serving experiments on Ascend NPUs; useful for HBM capacity provisioning rather than a purely abstract cache model.

title: Multimodal Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Vision-Language Models via Joint Pixel-Prompt Optimization
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / availability security / resource exhaustion / latency and energy amplification
why: 7d lower-rank systematic replay recovered a serving-security paper with unusually direct measured system impact. JPPO jointly optimizes image and visible prompt inputs; on open-source VLMs it reports over 4.6x latency and 5.3x energy amplification on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and over 36.6x latency with 32.7x energy amplification on BLIP-2, exposing a concrete multimodal-serving availability failure mode.

title: Muon-C: Operator-Aligned Muon for Convolutional Kernels
topic: distributed training/inference / optimizer / flow matching efficiency
why: Operator-aligned Muon for convolutional kernels reaches the final quality of unfolded Muon and Adam using 0.62x and 0.64x their model FLOPs on matched CIFAR-10 flow-matching experiments, with gains persisting across data scales and classification transfer.

title: Native LLM and MLLM Inference at Scale on Apple Silicon
topic: edge/on-device LLM and MLLM serving; Apple Silicon; MLX; continuous batching; prefix caching
why: Apple-Silicon serving canonical gap: vllm-mlx provides native MLX continuous batching plus content-based multimodal prefix caching; reports 21-87% higher text throughput than llama.cpp, 4.3x aggregate throughput at concurrency 16, and up to 28x repeated-image-query acceleration on M4 Max.

title: NUNA: Characterizing and Mitigating Non-Uniform Network Access in Multi-Die GPU Scale-Up Systems
topic: distributed inference / multi-die GPU / collectives / heterogeneous AI systems
why: Introduces non-uniform network access as a multi-die GPU scale-up bottleneck and proposes NUNA-aware routing plus placement. Reports up to 1.8x faster collectives and 7% mean / 28% max time-per-output-token speedup in ML inference. Direct AI-infra/architecture contribution.

title: OCGQuant: Outlier-Companion Grouping for NVFP4 Quantization
topic: quantization / NVFP4 / LLM inference / activation outliers
why: NVFP4-specific PTQ method that reduces collateral block quantization error by pairing outlier channels with low-magnitude companions. On Llama3/Qwen3 it reports the best evaluated perplexity/downstream accuracy while keeping prefill speedup close to RTN and matching RTN peak decoding memory.

title: OCTN: Neural OCT Representations for Robot-Guided Precision Intervention
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge/GPU runtime / robot-guided intervention
why: OCTN stores a continuous OCT tissue representation natively on GPU for fast geometric reasoning and robot integration. It reports up to 43x faster intensity-based spatial queries than conventional CPU processing, 4x lower acquisition time from sparse B-scans, sub-10s training, and demonstrates OCT-guided robotic laser surgery, making it strong protected Physical-AI runtime evidence.

title: Online Draft Co-Training for Speculative Decoding in Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training
topic: speculative decoding / RL post-training / context parallelism / pipeline parallelism
why: The system co-trains speculative drafts during large-scale RL rollout generation, extending packed zigzag-ring context parallelism with branch attention and adding TapChannel to move target features across pipeline stages without disturbing the pipeline schedule. It reports substantial rollout and end-to-end speedups up to 122B models, strong scaling to 256K context, memory savings, and modest PP transport overhead.

title: Optimizing CUDA like a Human: Micro-Profiling Tools as Expert Surrogates for LLM-Based GPU Kernel Optimization
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / agentic kernel optimization
why: KernelPro combines profiler-grounded multi-agent search with CuTe/CUDA generation; KernelBench reports 2.42x/4.69x/5.30x geometric-mean speedups on Levels 1/2/3 and measurable energy reduction.

title: Orla: A Library for Serving LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems; LLM serving; multi-agent runtime; workflow scheduling; KV cache management
why: Harvard Minlan Yu agent-serving canonical gap: serving layer above LLM engines separates workflow policy from request execution, with stage mapping, workflow orchestration and cross-workflow inference-state/KV-cache management; project page is author/lab official and links paper/code.

title: Osprey: Target-agnostic Pre-training Makes Stronger Drafters in Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / LLM inference acceleration / drafter training
why: Osprey pretrains a reusable target-agnostic shallow drafter backbone and adapts it to each target with lightweight vocabulary/QKV alignment and distillation. It improves mean acceptance length by 16.1% on Qwen3-8B, 21.2% on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and 22.7% on MiniMax-M2.5, with 17.5% higher tokens/s on the 229B MiniMax target; accepted at EMNLP 2026 with code released.

title: Ostrich: Taking Large Strides Through Stiff Contact in Differentiable Dynamics
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / GPU simulation / differentiable dynamics
why: Ostrich is a GPU-accelerated rigid-body differentiable simulator for stiff contact that uses large timesteps, implicit differentiation and Schur-complement reuse. It reports 211x faster warm iterations than MJX, 4.7x faster than Newton Semi-Implicit, 29x checkpointed-MJX optimization throughput, and 8,192 parallel worlds on one 24GB GPU, making it strong Physical-AI simulation infrastructure.

title: OUTLETS: Output-Length Prediction from Speculative Decoding Backbones
topic: LLM serving / speculative decoding / output-length prediction / scheduling
why: Repurposes latent representations already produced by speculative decoding draft backbones as a trajectory-aware output-length predictor. Under saturated disaggregated serving, its predictions improve standard scheduling and reduce short-request P99 latency by 34.8% while adding only a lightweight regression head when the draft backbone is already in use.

title: PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / visual token efficiency
why: Training-free VLM inference acceleration across both vision encoder and LLM. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, retains 93.8% performance with 10% visual tokens and reports 3.1x TTFT speedup.

title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving
topic: LLM serving / RAG serving / Physical AI cloud-edge runtime / dialogue systems
why: PACE jointly controls response-source routing, filler content and volatility-aware cache admission and is deployed on a humanoid-robot sales service. On 75k CarQA requests it halves pure-LLM P95 perceived time-to-first-response (0.29 vs 0.53s at c16), reaches 0.41s P95 and 2.4x lower latency than RAG at high load with equal quality, cuts filler calls by 94%, and eliminates stale answers in the reported setup.

title: PALS: Power-Aware LLM Serving for Mixture-of-Experts Models
topic: LLM serving; MoE systems; energy-efficient serving; power-aware runtime; QoS
why: Harvard Minlan Yu infrastructure canonical gap: vLLM-based runtime jointly controls GPU power caps and batch size using offline power-performance models plus online feedback; reports up to 26.3% better energy efficiency and 4x-7x fewer QoS violations under power constraints.

title: Parallelism Strategy Chaining for Fast Training Convergence
topic: distributed training/inference / parallelism / online adaptation
why: CONA observes that the best data/tensor/pipeline strategy changes during training and switches strategies online using a throughput-and-gradient surrogate. Across GPT-3 1.3B, BERT-Large and Llama-3.2-1B it reaches target perplexity 1.4-9.6x faster than prior strategy-selection methods.

title: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-context / parallel inference
why: PARSER decouples document reading from reasoning using frozen chunk-local subagents and iterative scatter-gather lead-agent reasoning. On 7K-896K-token multi-hop QA it improves quality while reducing inference latency by up to 11x versus sequential memory agents, making it a strong efficient-agent inference result.

title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling
topic: LLM serving / speculative decoding / edge inference / energy-aware runtime
why: PELM jointly controls DVFS, speculative decoding and variable verification depth for thermally constrained on-device LLM inference. Across hardware platforms and datasets it reports up to 23.1% speedup and 52.4% energy reduction over prior power-governing methods at comparable task quality; accepted to SenSys 2026 with an official open-source artifact.

title: PENDA: An Efficient Processing Element via Norm-of-Difference for Deep Learning Accelerators
topic: AI accelerator / processing element / arithmetic architecture / energy efficiency
why: Exact norm-of-difference processing element uses the law of cosines to replace conventional multiply-accumulate datapaths without approximation. Reported PE-array reductions are 11-36% area, 5-48% energy, and 11-19% clock period.

title: Poseidon: DAG-Guided Parallelism Search for LLM Pre-Training on Heterogeneous Clusters
topic: distributed training/inference / heterogeneous clusters / parallelism search
why: Poseidon builds an explicit DAG training-time model and prunes the parallelism search space with stage-level early stopping and layer-to-stage mapping. On heterogeneous accelerator clusters it improves LLM training throughput by up to 2.76x over state-of-the-art systems.

title: Positional task conditioning for scalable defect detection across product families in large product catalogs
topic: LLM serving / distillation / production inference cost
why: Decomposes long-context defect detection into focused tasks and distills the capability into one smaller model. PTC stays within 1.79% F1 of the frontier at up to 98% lower cost and is deployed across multiple countries processing more than 10 million product families.

title: Predict, Don't Iterate: Efficient Adaptive-Length Infilling for Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language models / inference acceleration / adaptive decoding
why: PILL removes preset-length search and avoids repeated multi-step denoising confidence probes for DLM infilling; across five DLMs and eight benchmarks it improves quality while running 1.82x faster than the strongest dynamic-length baseline.

title: PV-WM: A Heterogeneous Micro-Macro World Model for Articulated Pedestrian-Vehicle Co-Rollout
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world model / efficient rollout
why: PV-WM jointly rolls out articulated pedestrians and vehicles with a single recurrent model. Relative to a modular specialist it uses 57.1% fewer parameters, 96.5% lower average FLOPs per local scene and 25.5% lower measured p95 latency while improving forecast errors, giving direct efficient world-model evidence.

title: Q-ARVD: Quantizing Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models
topic: video generation acceleration; autoregressive video diffusion; quantization; Triton kernels
why: NUS xML canonical miss: targets frame-wise error accumulation and heterogeneous weight outliers in autoregressive video diffusion; reports INT8 deployment gains with Triton kernels and near-lossless quantized generation.

title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction
topic: quantization / quantization-aware training / low-bit LLM deployment / NVFP4
why: QUASAR is a current low-bit LLM QAT method that continuously performs lightweight loss-aware reconstruction inside training, supports standard integer/NVFP4 deployment with no inference-time changes, and improves held-out KL and downstream accuracy at 2-4 bits over strong QAT/PTQ baselines. It is directly relevant to Efficient ML low-precision deployment.

title: RAC: Reference-Aware Activation Compression for Communication-Efficient Split LLM Inference
topic: distributed inference / edge-cloud / activation compression
why: Direct split-inference communication optimization for privacy-sensitive LLM agents; reference-aware boundary activation coding reports 1.24-2.72x TTFT and 1.01-2.79x TPOT improvements across evaluated model-link pairs.

title: RAFM-SER++: A Lightweight Multimodal Emotion Recognition Framework for Real-Time Behavioral Monitoring in Surveillance Systems
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / lightweight asymmetric fusion / real-time inference
why: Replaces interaction-heavy bidirectional multimodal fusion with one-directional residual attention. Reports >60% fewer trainable parameters, 79.60 it/s inference, and strong BACC on IEMOCAP/ESD; direct measured accuracy-efficiency evidence.

title: Ragged Paged Attention: A High-Performance and Flexible LLM Inference Kernel for TPU
topic: efficient attention / TPU inference / JAX-Pallas
why: Pallas/Mosaic ragged paged-attention kernel for dynamic LLM serving on TPU with fine-grained tiling, fused KV update+attention software pipeline and workload-specialized compilation.

title: Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning
topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning / LLM serving
why: Training-free random per-head KV eviction that preserves prompts and exploits redundancy in reasoning traces; across four models and six reasoning tasks it matches the strongest prior evictor while serving 32-43% higher throughput in vLLM. Direct systems evidence and official SalesforceAIResearch code make this canonical-high.

title: Realtime-VLA FLASH: Speculative Inference Framework for Diffusion-based VLAs
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / speculative inference / diffusion action head / Triton kernels
why: Speculative inference system for diffusion VLAs using a lightweight draft model, parallel main-model verification and fallback; official implementation includes customized Triton serving kernels and reports ~3.04x task-level speedup.

title: RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory
topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive compute / latent recurrence
why: Adaptive latent-depth reasoning adds loop-time memory and a learned halting head. On MathQA it reaches 56.9% accuracy with 2.0 average loops, beating the best fixed-depth result by 2.2 points at matched compute; CALM needs 5.6 loops for 54.1%, while stronger adaptive baselines use 2.1-3.2 loops for lower accuracy. It also improves same-budget generation across 0.6B-8B models, directly supporting adaptive-compute efficiency.

title: RedKnot-MLA: Multi-Head Offline-Online Reuse for DeepSeek-V4 Long-Context Serving
topic: LLM serving / KV cache reuse / MLA / long context
why: RedKnot-MLA adapts head-aware offline-online reuse to packed MLA without splitting the latent KV stream. Frozen operating points report 2.02-3.84x hot-artifact TTFT speedups and about 2.0x preliminary 256K QPS, with 78.7-79.5% analytic major-operator arithmetic saving at 256K.

title: Reducing Temporal Redundancy for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
topic: Physical AI; VLA inference; temporal redundancy; visual token reuse; diffusion action acceleration
why: SJTU EPIC protected Physical-AI canonical miss: incrementally updates dynamic visual tokens and compresses diffusion action sampling to two steps, reporting over 2x VLA inference speedup while maintaining high manipulation success.

title: Redwood: A Frontier AI Accelerator Designed, Verified, and Deployed from Scratch in 2 Weeks by AI
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / Physical AI accelerator
why: End-to-end hardware/software co-designed accelerator for low-power low-latency Physical-AI inference. Projected Samsung 8nm results report 1.75x throughput and 1.9x lower power versus measured Jetson Orin Nano baseline, or 3.4x perf/W.

title: Rethinking Network Topologies for Cost-Effective Mixture-of-Experts LLM Serving
topic: MoE systems / LLM serving / interconnect topology / cost efficiency
why: Cross-layer study of XPU network topology for MoE LLM serving. Compares scale-up, scale-out, 3D torus and 3D full-mesh and reports 20.6-56.2% higher cost-effectiveness for lower-cost switchless topologies across studied scenarios, with up to 27% throughput-per-cost improvement from reducing over-provisioned link bandwidth.

title: Revati: Transparent GPU-Free Time-Warp Emulation for LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving; systems emulation; performance modeling; vLLM; SGLang; infrastructure optimization
why: Georgia Tech SAIL/Alexey Tumanov canonical infrastructure gap: transparent CUDA-API time-warp emulation executes real vLLM/SGLang serving control logic without GPUs, achieving <5% prediction error while running 5-17x faster than real GPU execution and enabling low-cost configuration-space exploration.

title: RGB Input Pipelines: Throughput, GPU Memory, and Transformation Coverage
topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / data pipeline / training systems / input preprocessing
why: 7d replay recovered a focused systems benchmark of seven RGB input paths from five libraries, measuring synchronized CUDA float16 batch throughput and peak GPU memory over 759 measurements on an NVIDIA L4. DALI and AlbumentationsX reach median 5,029 and 4,679 images/s on shared recipes; DALI is 1.18x median faster on 22 shared recipes. The work provides actionable coverage/performance evidence and benchmark code for a frequently overlooked training/inference input bottleneck.

title: RippleKV: Cross-Layer KV Cache Allocation via Perturbation Propagation
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / cross-layer cache allocation
why: Quality-gated 30d true miss. RippleKV allocates a fixed global KV-cache budget across layers by measuring how norm-adaptive perturbations injected into each layer value cache propagate to the final predictive distribution. The resulting offline downstream-sensitivity profile is converted to non-uniform layer budgets while preserving the total cache budget. LongBench experiments report the strongest average performance among evaluated KV-compression methods under matched budgets, with no online profiling overhead. This is directly relevant to long-context inference memory efficiency and fills a cross-layer allocation neighborhood missed by the earlier 30d scan.

title: RoLA: Rotary-Positioned Low-Rank Linear Attention for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
topic: video/image generation acceleration / diffusion/flow acceleration / efficient attention
why: RoLA places RoPE outside a nonlinear low-rank feature map so the global branch keeps a reusable linear summary while preserving relative rotary geometry. On Wan2.1-14B video generation at 720p/81 frames on H100, the sparse-low-rank module remains competitive at 90% sparsity and achieves 2.63x measured end-to-end inference speedup.

title: RT-HiSS: Ray Tracing Accelerated High Dimensional Vector Similarity Searches
topic: GPU kernel/accelerators / vector search / heterogeneous GPU cores
why: Direct heterogeneous-GPU acceleration contribution that repurposes RT cores for exact high-dimensional similarity search with CUDA refinement, batching, shared-memory tiling and compressed result masks; reports up to 8.37x over competitive GPU algorithms and up to 2368.26x over brute force across six real-world datasets.

title: RTP-LLM: High-Performance Alibaba LLM Inference Engine
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / speculative decoding / quantization / multimodal serving
why: Alibaba production-serving canonical gap: production LLM inference engine serving 100M+ users, integrating file-order model loading, prefill-decode disaggregation, hierarchical KV caching, modular speculative decoding, adaptive KV quantization and multimodal decoupling; reports 4.7-6.3x loading speedup and substantial latency/throughput gains over vLLM/SGLang.

title: S2-MoE: Enabling Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts on Edge Devices
topic: speculative decoding / MoE systems / edge inference / llama.cpp
why: Direct edge-AI inference contribution combining routing-aware adaptive speculative expansion, reuse-aware expert gating, and shared-context self-speculation for MoE. Implemented in llama.cpp; reports up to 5.3x and about 2.0x average speedup across evaluated MoE models/tasks, with Jetson Orin and RTX 4090 evaluation.

title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / sparse attention / disaggregated memory / CXL

Evaluated with DeepSeek-V3.2/SGLang, reporting 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT, and 1.8x lower TBT versus RDMA baselines.

title: SAGE: Semantic-Aware Geographic Error Recovery for AI Data Movement
topic: distributed training/inference / AI interconnect / fault recovery / communication latency
why: Semantic-aware replay architecture distinguishes catastrophic from quantization-like numerical faults and adapts replay restart geography. gem5 Garnet plus ASAP7 evaluation reports 30.1% lower quality-normalized terminal latency than fixed 34-hop recovery, including 28.0% lower mean latency, bounded queues under higher-BER stress, and lower DeiT-S mean/p99.5 latency.

title: SageBwd: A Trainable Low-bit Attention
topic: efficient attention; low-bit training; INT8 attention; pretraining
why: Fresh SageAttention/Jianfei Chen neighborhood recheck surfaced an uncatalogued low-bit attention paper. SageBwd studies trainable INT8 attention, identifies backward score-gradient quantization as the main error source, and shows settings that match full-precision attention during pretraining.

title: Sample-Guided Exact Top-K Selection for Long-Context Sparse Attention
topic: efficient attention / sparse attention / GPU kernel
why: HPC-Ops Top-K uses fixed-stride sampling only to propose a coarse boundary while a mandatory full-row pass certifies correctness, then performs exact FP32 refinement with graph-capturable ragged dispatch. On Hy4-Preview indexer scores it beats the fastest verified exact baseline by 1.29-1.75x across 20 operator configurations (1.55x geometric mean) and gives 1.36x/1.48x on framework traces.

topic: LLM serving / diffusion language models / scheduling / disaggregated serving
why: Serving system for cached diffusion LLMs. Deficit token-budget scheduling handles indivisible recurrent prefills; colocated/disaggregated/hybrid execution addresses dLLM prefill-decode interference and partitioning. Official UT-InfraAI implementation is available.

KAN data-parallel training reaches 5.97x speedup and 74.7% parallel efficiency at 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs across 4 nodes, with communication overhead characterized at 1.3%-6.1%. This is concrete distributed-training systems evidence rather than only an algorithmic KAN paper.

title: Scalable Context Orchestration for Serving LLMs Over Voice

why: Direct serving middleware for bounded voice-specific context and runtime directives. Real-world evaluation reports 79.2% lower model usage cost and up to 24.9x lower per-turn cost in long sessions while retaining up to 98.7% baseline answer quality.

title: Scalable Edge-assisted Fusion and Path Prediction for Connected Autonomous Vehicles
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge-cloud heterogeneous AI / connected autonomous vehicles
why: Conductor moves multi-vehicle world-model fusion and trajectory prediction to the edge, combines an occlusion-aware input selector with a runtime controller, and dynamically adapts both AV input count and prediction work to stay inside a strict Age-of-Information budget. Primary-source evaluation reports the AoI safety bound is met across scenarios with up to 31 CAVs while preserving fusion fidelity close to an Oracle and substantially above random selection under the same deadline, providing direct systems evidence for protected Physical-AI cloud-edge runtime design.

title: Scale-QLoRA: Code-Invariant Adapter Merging for Native 4-bit Microscaling LLMs
topic: quantization / native 4-bit microscaling / LoRA deployment / code-invariant merge
why: 30d quantization deployment replay recovered a paper absent from the current authority/watch union. It targets a concrete deployment problem for NVFP4/MXFP4 checkpoints: conventional LoRA merging can re-derive the discrete code plane and erase adaptation. Scale-QLoRA freezes the E2M1 code plane and adapts only per-block scales on the deployment grid, making merge bit-exact within the native format while removing runtime adapter overhead and enabling exact rollback/deduplication.

title: Scaling E-Commerce Attribute Extraction with Parallel Decoding
topic: LLM serving / parallel decoding / production inference cost
why: A compact Qwen3-4B extractor with Hyper-Parallel Decoding reaches 85% extraction accuracy, on par with the foundational LLM teacher, while reducing inference cost by 92%. The pipeline is explicitly designed for production-scale catalog extraction, providing direct measured serving-efficiency evidence.

title: SceneMosaic: Efficient and Diverse Simulation-Ready Scene Generation via Hybrid Agentic Layout Evolution
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / simulation infrastructure / agentic generation

On SceneEval-100 it matches the strongest agentic baseline in semantic layout quality with a 24x speedup while reducing physical violations, making it strong embodied-simulation generation infrastructure.

The paper reports 53.3% and 43.6% rollout-throughput gains over tuned cache-aware vLLM Router in rollout-only tests, and 35.6% higher throughput with 22.8% lower mean iteration time in a matched training experiment while preserving the requested workload mixture.

title: SemBridge: Compiling Consumer Observations into Cross-Stack Communication Plans
topic: distributed training/inference / compiler / heterogeneous communication
why: SemBridge compiles consumer-visible distributed-tensor obligations into backend-neutral communication plans across CUDA/NCCL and CANN/HCCL. On a measured two-host 1-GbE deployment, source projection cuts result traffic by >99.97% and improves throughput by 8.92-80.20% across Dense, MoE and MiniMax workloads, providing direct systems evidence.

topic: KV cache/long-context / quantization
why: Direct long-context inference memory optimization. Measures the KV quality cliff and uses semantic mixed precision above it; reports 6.0x KV storage reduction with no statistically detectable quality difference and up to 7.9x with distortion-optimized quantization.

topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / reasoning offload / graph runtime / enterprise agents

The implementation loads a 24M-edge authentication subgraph in 14.2 minutes, roughly 24x faster than the canonical MERGE pipeline; alerts trigger within <=2.5 s and the integrated containment loop has 6.3 s median completion.

title: SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching
topic: LLM/recommendation serving / ultra-long sequence / low-rank caching / fused kernel
why: SequenceO1 is deployed at full traffic on Douyin for histories up to 100K interactions. Its compress-then-reason design combines target-agnostic sketches, target-conditioned cross attention, low-rank user-representation caching, multi-request batching, pipeline lift, and a fused FlashSA kernel to amortize storage, communication, and compute across online requests.

title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / Physical-AI protected
why: Streaming MLLM system that uses shallow-layer KV as an always-on retrieval index and invokes deeper computation only for selected evidence; reports up to 52.1x lower per-frame prefill latency and 11.9x lower 10-second end-to-end latency while matching strong streaming baselines.

title: Sharing a Fabric with Collective Communication: Two Storage Penalties in Deep Learning Training
topic: distributed training/inference / storage / collective communication
why: This work isolates DataLoader stalls and collective contention when storage I/O shares the training fabric with NCCL/RCCL. Node-local NVMe staging via DYAD removes both effects, yielding a 7.4x epoch speedup over direct Lustre reads and 1.31x over VAST after cache warmup.

title: Shift-Accumulate Attention: Multiplier-Free Query--Key Products for Transformer Decoding
topic: quantization / efficient attention / KV cache / GPU kernels
why: Signed power-of-two KV coding turns QK products into sign/shift/integer accumulation and also uses shift-exact online softmax and log-quantized AV. Fused RTX 4090 kernels report 4.60x speedup over FP16 SDPA at B=8,T=32k with 2.5x smaller KV cache; an iso-storage control isolates 2.02x arithmetic benefit, while the paper explicitly notes matched INT8 MAC can be faster on current GPU hardware.

title: SHIFT: Surface-aware High-speed Integration For TSDFs
topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robotic mapping / memory-efficient runtime
why: SHIFT reduces redundant online TSDF/ESDF updates by compressing flat regions into super-rays, freezing converged gradients and using a compact ESDF layout. Across RGB-D and LiDAR sequences it cuts TSDF cost by 1.42-4.07x while preserving millimeter-scale mesh error and lowers ESDF memory by up to 28%, directly targeting real-time robotic mapping.

title: Simthesizer: An Agent-Driven Simulation Framework for LLM Serving Systems
topic: LLM serving / serving simulator / agentic workloads / disaggregated serving / speculative decoding / KV cache
why: Introduces a composable dynamic-DAG simulator plus agent-driven lowering for rapidly evolving LLM serving mechanisms. It explicitly models agentic multi-call/tool workflows, disaggregated serving, KV-cache quantization and speculative decoding; extensions track a vLLM-based real system with 2.51% average throughput error versus 6.03% for extensions on existing simulators, while simulation is up to 284.96x/23.19x faster than LLMServingSim2.0/Vidur. Direct AI-infra systems contribution with public implementation.

The paper reports 9.6x denoising speedup and end-to-end latency reduction from 274 ms to 83 ms on pi0.5, and 3.56x end-to-end acceleration on SmolVLA while preserving or improving task quality.

Across seven LVLMs and 18 image/video benchmarks, LLaVA-Video-7B reduces visual tokens by 90.5%, retains 92.7% of baseline performance, and achieves a measured 2.24x inference speedup.

why: ISTA DASLab canonical miss: formalizes task- and distribution-lossless quantization, introduces EAR fidelity, and reports task-lossless compression below 4 bits plus 1.7-3.6x inference speedups with optimized kernels.

title: TEFM: Token-Efficient Faithful Modeling for Structured Data

why: ICML 2026 official Downloads inventory paper. Establishes a bits-to-rounds principle for masked diffusion language models and proposes training-free Explore-Then-Exploit parallel decoding, directly reducing decoding rounds and inference compute.

Introduces learned shared memory for parallel agent teams so useful intermediate steps can be reused across trajectories while controlling context growth, reducing redundant computation and runtime while matching or improving task quality on AssistantBench and GAIA; official UCF implementation verified.

title: Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism: Load Balancing An Imbalanced Mixture-of-Experts
topic: MoE systems / expert parallelism / distributed inference / load balancing
why: ICML 2026 system/algorithmic infrastructure work for imbalanced MoE expert parallelism. LLEP dynamically reroutes excess tokens together with expert parameters to underutilized devices; authors report up to 5x speedup and 4x lower peak memory versus standard EP, including about 1.9x faster full-model inference for gpt-oss-120b.

title: Less Is More: Training-Free Sparse Attention with Global Locality for Efficient Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / sparse attention / KV-cache decoding
why: ICML 2026; training-free cross-head unified sparse attention for long reasoning. Official author/Princeton pages confirm acceptance; reports lossless AIME-24 accuracy with up to 87.5% fewer attended tokens and about 1.13x end-to-end generation speedup.

title: Less Token, More Signal: MoE Expert Pruning via Critical Token Selection
topic: MoE systems / expert pruning / memory-efficient inference
why: ICML 2026 Poster. STEP uses critical-token-guided expert importance with loss-aware evaluation and lightweight knowledge preservation; on Qwen3-30B with 50% expert sparsity it nearly halves memory, improves throughput by about 1.5x, and completes pruning in under 10 minutes.

title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / PTQ / long-form generation quality
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit LLM PTQ paper addressing long-generation quality degradation through logit-aware final-block quantization; complements block-wise PTQ and reasoning-focused deployment routes.

title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width Control for Pareto-Optimal LLM Deployment
topic: quantization / fractional bit-width / memory-constrained LLM deployment
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Continuous effective bit-width enables Pareto-optimal LLM fitting under exact GPU memory budgets; a 70B model can be fit at ~2.4 bits with a hardware-friendly decoding path.

title: Light Forcing: Accelerating Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Sparse Attention
topic: video generation acceleration / autoregressive video / sparse attention / kernels
why: ICML 2026 direct video-generation efficiency work; chunk-aware hierarchical sparse attention gives ~1.2-1.3x E2E alone and ~2-3x with deployment optimizations; official repository provides sparse kernels and quantized deployment paths.

title: LightningRL: Breaking the Accuracy-Parallelism Trade-off of Block-wise dLLMs via Reinforcement Learning
topic: diffusion LLM / parallel decoding / RL post-training / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 direct dLLM acceleration; RL optimizes speed-quality Pareto frontier and the official implementation reports 336 TPS on H100, ~3.2x faster than SDAR while maintaining high accuracy.

title: LiME: Lightweight Mixture of Experts for Efficient Multimodal Multi-task Learning
topic: multimodal efficiency / lightweight MoE / parameter-efficient fine-tuning / adaptive routing
why: ICML 2026 multimodal-efficiency work. LiME replaces per-expert adapter replication with shared PEFT plus lightweight expert modulation and zero-parameter routing, using up to 4x fewer trainable parameters and up to 29% faster training than MoE-PEFT baselines.

title: LiMuon: Light and Fast Muon Optimizer for Large Models
topic: LLM training efficiency / memory-efficient optimizer / Muon
why: ICML 2026; lowers Muon optimizer memory with randomized SVD and improves stochastic sample complexity via variance reduction, with experiments on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B and ViT showing practical training-efficiency gains.

title: LK Losses: Direct Acceptance Rate Optimization for Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / draft-model training / acceptance optimization
why: ICML 2026. Replaces KL-proxy draft training with acceptance-aligned LK objectives; across four draft architectures and six target models (8B-685B), improves average acceptance length by up to about 8-10% with no inference overhead and integrates directly into existing speculator training pipelines.

title: Locally Coherent Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / parallel decoding / local autoregressive decoding / efficient code generation / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-track paper from IBM Research/ETH Zurich. CoDiLA combines global diffusion-LM parallel generation with a compact local autoregressive decoder operating on diffusion latents, preserving sub-linear generation latency while repairing local syntactic dependencies that otherwise break parallel decoding. It establishes an improved accuracy-speed Pareto frontier for code generation and is a direct diffusion-LM parallel-decoding efficiency work.

title: LoKiFormer: Locality-aware Attention with Decoupled Knowledge Memory for Efficient Large Language Model Pretraining
topic: LLM pretraining efficiency / efficient attention / explicit knowledge memory
why: ICML 2026; introduces Local Fusion Attention plus a decoupled parametric Knowledge Memory Module to reduce redundant local modeling and separate knowledge storage from computation; reports 1.33x faster pretraining convergence than Transformer baselines.

title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
topic: efficient attention / long-context LLM inference / on-device inference
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight; DHSA predicts content-dependent sparse attention online with variable-length hierarchical routing and memory-efficient GPU/CPU backends; reports up to 10x prefill speedup at 128K and enables 100K context on a single 24GB GPU while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LoSA: Locality Aware Sparse Attention for Block-Wise Diffusion Language Models
topic: efficient attention / diffusion language model acceleration / KV reuse / sparse attention / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026. Addresses KV Inflation in block-wise diffusion language models by reusing cached prefix-attention for stable tokens and applying sparse attention only to active tokens. It reports 1.54x lower attention density and up to 4.14x attention speedup on RTX A6000 while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LRAgent: Efficient KV Cache Sharing for Multi-LoRA LLM Agents
topic: KV cache sharing / multi-LoRA agent serving / Flash-LoRA-Attention
why: Multi-LoRA agent serving framework that decomposes KV cache into a shared base component plus low-rank adapter-dependent cache; reports up to 2.46x throughput, 4.44x TTFT reduction and about 3x KV-cache memory reduction while preserving accuracy.

title: LSGQuant: Layer-Sensitivity Guided Quantization for One-Step Diffusion Real-World Video Super-Resolution
topic: quantization / video generation acceleration / diffusion transformer / low-bit inference
why: ICML 2026 direct diffusion/video quantization work. Layer-sensitivity guided PTQ combines dynamic-range-aware activation quantization, variance-oriented layer training, and quantization-aware optimization to compress one-step DiT video super-resolution while preserving near-full-precision quality; author publication page and ICML listing confirm venue, and official author repository is verified.

title: LUGS: Latent-aware Guidance for Efficient Unmasking in Diffusion Large Language Models
topic: diffusion language model acceleration / efficient decoding / unmasking policy / latent guidance
why: ICML 2026 poster. Direct dLLM inference-efficiency work: uses latent hidden-state guidance to improve unmasking decisions beyond local confidence/entropy heuristics, targeting better quality-efficiency trade-offs in parallel diffusion decoding.

title: M+Adam: Low-Precision Training via Additive-Multiplicative Optimization
topic: low-precision training / FP8 FP4 / optimizer / memory efficiency
why: ICML 2026. Combines additive and multiplicative updates to train directly with BF16, FP8, and FP4 master weights without higher-precision copies; improves low-precision LLaMA-style pretraining across model scales and budgets.

title: ManifoldKV: Training-Free KV Cache Compression via Euclidean Outlier Detection
topic: KV cache compression / training-free eviction / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 training-free KV compression using Euclidean outlier detection; improves multi-key retrieval robustness and restores 64K-context performance with windowed scoring while requiring minimal implementation changes.

title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving
topic: LLM serving / disaggregated inference / predictive scheduling / memory-aware scheduling
why: ICML 2026 Poster; device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud prefilling plus uncertainty-calibrated hierarchical scheduling for memory-bound disaggregated decode; reports 42.6% lower mean end-to-end latency and up to 84.8% lower tail latency versus three serving baselines.

title: MedCoG: Maximizing LLM Inference Density in Medical Reasoning via Meta-Cognitive Regulation
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / inference-time compute allocation / adaptive knowledge use
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Meta-cognitive regulation avoids indiscriminate inference scaling by adaptively deciding when and how to use procedural, episodic, and factual knowledge; reports roughly 5.5x inference density on difficult medical reasoning benchmarks.

title: MemOCR: Layout-Aware Visual Memory for Efficient Long-Horizon Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / agent memory / multimodal memory compression / long-horizon context efficiency
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by official/author sources and Meituan repository. MemOCR compresses growing interaction histories into adaptive visual layouts and reports about 8x token-efficiency gain under extreme budgets, making it a canonical context/memory-efficiency route for long-horizon agents.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Pretraining via Minimalist Optimizer Design
topic: distributed training / memory-efficient LLM pretraining / optimizer-state reduction
why: ICML 2026 memory-efficient LLM pretraining work. SCALE combines column-wise gradient normalization with first-order momentum only on the output layer, matching or exceeding Adam while using only about 35-45% of total memory across 60M-1B models and outperforming memory-efficient baselines such as GaLore/Fira/APOLLO; the official OptimAI-Lab repository provides the implementation.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Dynamic Sparsity: From Stability to Practical Scaling
topic: LLM training efficiency / dynamic sparsity / memory-efficient optimization
why: ICML 2026; Sparse Memory-Efficient Training stabilizes dynamic sparse LLM pretraining with optimizer warm-up and density-aware learning-rate scaling while storing gradients and optimizer states only for active parameters, making sparse pretraining materially memory-efficient.

title: Mining Tensor/Neuron-Level Sparsity to Maximize Mixture-of-Experts Potential in Post-Training and Inference
topic: MoE systems / post-training sparsity / token-expert dropping / expert partition / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper, with the same author set as the earlier arXiv title DualSparse-MoE. It exploits tensor-level and neuron-level sparsity after pretraining via expert partitioning, threshold-based token-expert dropping, partial partition/reconstruction, and load-imbalance-aware execution. Reported inference-only results reach up to 1.41x MoE speedup with under 0.5% accuracy loss, making it a direct MoE deployment-efficiency canonical.

title: MixFP4: Enhancing NVFP4 with Adaptive FP4/INT4 Block Representations
topic: quantization / FP4-INT4 micro-format / Tensor Core co-design / LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 poster. MixFP4 extends NVFP4 with per-block E2M1/E1M2 selection while reusing the FP8 block-scale sign bit for zero-extra-metadata format tagging and a unified internal compute representation; reports improved 4-bit robustness with only 3.1% area and 1.5% power overhead in the proposed Tensor Core support.

title: MixQuant: Pushing the Limits of Block Rotations in Post-Training Quantization
topic: quantization / post-training quantization / block Hadamard rotation / low-bit LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit PTQ work. MixQuant/PeRQ analyzes the limits of block Hadamard rotations and calibrates permutation-based activation-mass redistribution before rotation, then folds permutations into model weights so deployment adds no inference overhead; experiments recover up to about 90% of full-vector-rotation perplexity for INT4 Llama3-1B at block size 16.

title: Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers
topic: video generation acceleration / diffusion / dynamic sparse attention
why: ICML 2026 video-DiT efficiency work. MOD-DiT models evolving attention sparsity with a mixture-of-distributions approximation plus online block masking, avoiding repeated expensive sparsity sampling while preserving generation quality and accelerating video diffusion attention.

title: Model-Preserving Adaptive Rounding
topic: quantization / LLM PTQ / adaptive rounding / model-preserving compression
why: ICML 2026 Cornell RelaxML quantization paper introducing YAQA, an adaptive-rounding PTQ method using full-model/Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations rather than layer-local activation error. Primary arXiv reports about 30% lower KL divergence to the original model across models/quantizers with no inference overhead; official Christopher De Sa publication page lists it as ICML 2026.

title: MoSE: Mixture of Slimmable Experts for Efficient and Adaptive Language Models
topic: MoE / conditional computation / slimmable experts / adaptive inference FLOPs
why: ICML 2026 efficient-MoE work. MoSE makes each expert slimmable, allowing runtime control over both which experts execute and how much of each expert executes. It shifts the accuracy-compute Pareto frontier toward lower inference FLOPs and supports budget-aware runtime width selection.

title: MoshiRAG: Asynchronous Knowledge Retrieval for Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
topic: multimodal serving / full-duplex speech LM / asynchronous RAG / real-time inference
why: ICML 2026 real-time multimodal serving work. MoshiRAG keeps a compact full-duplex speech-language interface while asynchronously retrieving stronger knowledge sources during the natural response gap, improving factuality without sacrificing real-time interactivity; the official implementation includes production-oriented Rust inference code.

title: Motion-Aware Caching for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
topic: autoregressive video generation / cache reuse / diffusion acceleration
why: ICML 2026. MotionCache uses token-level motion-aware cache reuse instead of coarse chunk skipping; reports 6.28x on SkyReels-V2 and 1.64x on MAGI-1 with very small quality loss.

title: Multi-Head LatentMoE and Head Parallel: Communication-Efficient and Deterministic MoE Parallelism
topic: MoE systems / distributed training / communication-efficient parallelism / deterministic routing / IO-aware execution
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Multi-Head LatentMoE with Head Parallel achieves O(1) communication cost with respect to activated experts, fully balanced deterministic traffic, and IO-aware routing/expert computation; compared with MoE expert parallelism it reports up to 1.61x faster training at identical performance.

title: Multipole Semantic Attention: A Fast Approximation of Softmax Attention for Pretraining
topic: efficient attention / long-context pretraining / attention approximation
why: ICML 2026. Semantic clustering plus multipole expansions gives subquadratic/drop-in attention; reports 3x isolated-layer speedup over cuDNN FlashAttention at 8k and material end-to-end long-context pretraining runtime reductions with small loss degradation.

title: MVR-cache: Optimizing Semantic Caching via Multi-Vector Retrieval and Learned Prompt Segmentation
topic: LLM serving / semantic cache / response reuse / retrieval / inference cost reduction
why: ICML 2026 semantic-caching system for LLM serving. MVR-cache learns prompt segmentation and uses multi-vector retrieval/MaxSim to improve semantically safe response-cache reuse; experiments report up to 37% higher cache hit rate at the same correctness guarantee, directly reducing repeated LLM inference cost and latency.

title: NanoFLUX: Distillation-Driven Compression of Large Text-to-Image Generation Models for Mobile Devices
topic: image generation acceleration / flow matching / model compression / mobile edge AI / distillation
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists NanoFLUX as a main-conference paper. NanoFLUX progressively compresses FLUX.1-Schnell from a 17B teacher to a 2.4B mobile text-to-image model using DiT pruning, token downsampling, and text-encoder distillation, reporting 512x512 generation in about 2.5 seconds on a mobile device.

title: NanoQuant: Efficient Sub-1-Bit Quantization of Large Language Models
topic: quantization / sub-1-bit PTQ / custom kernels / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026. Sub-1-bit post-training quantization with custom low-bit kernels; reports extreme model-memory compression and practical consumer-GPU deployment while preserving useful accuracy.

title: NanoSpec: Accelerating Speculative Decoding using Minimalist In-Context Vocabularies
topic: speculative decoding / active-vocabulary pruning / GPU runtime
why: ICML 2026. Training-free speculative-decoding co-design that restricts draft computation to a small dynamic in-context vocabulary and combines asynchronous gathering/GPU-resident state to reduce draft cost and improve end-to-end speed.

title: Native Parallel Reasoner: Reasoning in Parallelism via Self-Distilled Reinforcement Learning
topic: efficient reasoning / parallel reasoning / SGLang runtime / reinforcement learning / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. NPR trains models to reason with genuine parallel execution rather than serial autoregressive traces; its NPR Engine refactors SGLang memory/flow control for parallel RL and inference, reporting up to 4.6x inference acceleration across reasoning benchmarks.

title: NeUQI: Near-Optimal Uniform Quantization Parameter Initialization for Low-Bit LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / low-bit PTQ / uniform quantization / parameter initialization / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by the senior-author publication list. NeUQI replaces suboptimal Min-Max initialization with efficient near-optimal initialization for uniform low-bit PTQ and is designed to improve practical memory/decoding efficiency on consumer-grade hardware.

title: No Retraining at Edge: Efficient Resource-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization via Federated Supernet Learning
topic: edge AI / mixed-precision quantization / federated supernet / resource-adaptive deployment
why: ICML 2026 Poster. DFMPQ trains a weight-sharing mixed-precision federated supernet once, then derives resource-aware quantized subnets for changing edge constraints without retraining; directly targets heterogeneous edge deployment cost.

title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable
topic: distributed LLM training / optimizer / FSDP2 / training efficiency
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Neuron-wise normalized Muon with a distributed FSDP2 implementation; Microsoft reports 21.74% better training efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on 1.1B pretraining with comparable memory footprint.

title: Not All Prefills Are Equal: PPD Disaggregation for Multi-turn LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / prefill-decode disaggregation / multi-turn KV reuse
why: ICML 2026; dynamic PPD routing reuses cached KV for Turn 2+ append-prefill on decode nodes and reports about 68% lower Turn 2+ TTFT while controlling TPOT and KV-transfer congestion.

title: OBCache: Optimal Brain KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / output-aware eviction / pruning
why: ICML 2026. Formulates KV eviction as structured pruning using output-aware Optimal-Brain-Damage saliency; plug-and-play with H2O/TOVA/SnapKV/AdaKV and consistently improves long-context eviction quality. Official code is built on NVIDIA KVPress.

title: On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / tool calling / RL training efficiency / rollout efficiency / wall-clock acceleration
why: ICML 2026. Identifies wasted rollout compute from zero-learning-signal prompts and high policy-update cost in RL-based tool-calling training, then introduces complementary techniques that substantially accelerate wall-clock training without degrading tool-calling performance; also audits evaluation-pipeline instability.

title: On Efficient Scaling of GNNs via IO-Aware Layers Implementations
topic: GPU kernel / graph neural network systems / IO-aware layers / sparse attention / SpMM / hardware-efficient training and inference
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Develops IO-aware GPU kernels for SpMM, reductions, GATv2 and Graph Transformer layers; reports up to 8.5x GATv2 speedup, 7.3x Tensor-Core Graph-Transformer speedup on locally dense graphs, and up to 76x peak-memory reduction, with drop-in implementations.

title: Online Linear Programming for Multi-Objective Routing in LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / request routing / SLO optimization / KV-cache-aware scheduling
why: ICML 2026 LLM-serving routing framework formulated as online linear programming under batch-size and KV-cache constraints, with warm-started dual updates for millisecond decisions and improved latency/TTFT/throughput/tail metrics in Vidur.

title: Optimal Self-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning with Large Language Models
topic: efficient reasoning / test-time scaling / adaptive sampling / self-consistency
why: ICML 2026. Blend-ASC dynamically allocates self-consistency samples under arbitrary budgets and uses 6.8x fewer samples than vanilla self-consistency on average while maintaining reasoning performance.

title: OSAQ: Outlier Self-Absorption for Accurate Low-bit LLM Quantization
topic: LLM quantization / weight-only low-bit PTQ / outlier suppression
why: ICML 2026. Closed-form Hessian-null-space additive transformation suppresses weight outliers offline with no inference overhead; substantially improves 2-bit GPTQ perplexity.

title: OServe: Accelerating LLM Serving via Spatial-Temporal Workload Orchestration
topic: LLM serving / heterogeneous deployment / scheduling

title: ParisKV: Fast and Drift-Robust KV-Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / GPU retrieval / CPU offload
why: GPU-native drift-robust KV-cache retrieval with collision-based candidate selection, 4-bit reranking and UVA CPU offload; reports up to 2.8x higher throughput in the full-attention runnable range and 17x/44x lower decode latency than MagicPIG/PQCache at million-token scale. Official ICML 2026 poster/slides and arXiv identity verified.

title: PatternKV: Flattening KV Representation Expands Quantization Headroom
topic: KV cache / quantization / long-context inference / test-time scaling
why: ICML 2026 direct KV-cache quantization work. Pattern-aligned residual quantization flattens native KV distributions before low-bit coding; reports near-lossless 4-bit behavior, stronger 2-bit quality, about 10% average test-time-scaling accuracy gain, 1.4x throughput, and 1.25x larger supported batches.

title: PETS: A Principled Framework Towards Optimal Trajectory Allocation for Efficient Test-Time Self-Consistency
topic: efficient reasoning / test-time scaling / adaptive trajectory allocation
why: ICML 2026; principled offline/online allocation of reasoning trajectories under a sampling budget; reports up to 75% lower offline and 55% lower online sampling budget for the same self-consistency target.

title: PinTok: Tokenizers Deserve Dedicated Pinned CPU-Compute and Memory
topic: LLM serving / tokenizer runtime / CPU pinning / latency-sensitive inference
why: ICML 2026; treats tokenization as a first-class serving bottleneck and reduces OS scheduling, context-switch, memory-placement, and packet-copy overhead via dedicated pinned CPU compute and memory.

title: PipeSD: An Efficient Cloud-Edge Collaborative Pipeline Inference Framework with Speculative Decoding
topic: cloud-edge LLM inference / speculative decoding / pipeline scheduling
why: ICML 2026; real cloud-edge testbed combining token-batch pipelining and adaptive verification triggering; reports 1.16x-2.16x speedup and 14.3%-25.3% energy reduction.

title: Plan for Speed: Dilated Scheduling for Masked Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / parallel decoding / inference-only scheduling / generation acceleration
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads inventory paper. Proposes an inference-only dilated unmasking scheduler that parallelizes masked-diffusion generation without retraining and explicitly targets the speed-quality frontier.

title: PLASH: Provably Linear-Time Attention with Selective Higher-Order Feature Sketching
topic: efficient attention / long-context / linear-time attention / feature sketching
why: ICML 2026 official poster. Compresses keys/values into learned prototypes with polynomial feature enrichment and provides linear-time runtime bounds, directly targeting long-context training and inference cost.

title: PLoRA: Efficient Concurrent LoRA Training for Large Language Models
topic: LLM training systems / LoRA / GPU utilization / concurrent training / custom kernels
why: ICML 2026 main-conference systems paper confirmed by author publication pages and the official inventory. Orchestrates concurrent LoRA fine-tuning jobs and custom GPU kernels, reporting up to 12.8x training throughput and 7.52x shorter makespan.

title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
topic: distributed LLM training / memory-efficient optimizer / Triton kernels
why: ICML 2026 Oral. Scalable orthogonal-equivalence training with input-centric reconstruction, structured/blockwise transforms and kernel engineering; enables billion-parameter pretraining on a single H100 where AdamW OOMs and materially improves memory/throughput over original POET.

title: PRAC: Principal-Random Subspace for LLM Activation Compression and Memory-Efficient Training
topic: distributed training / activation compression / memory-efficient LLM training
why: ICML 2026 direct memory-efficient LLM training work. PRAC decomposes activations into principal and random subspaces, yields an unbiased low-variance gradient estimator, and reports up to 36% total memory reduction with negligible quality loss. ICML Downloads and senior-author publication page confirm acceptance.

title: Predicting Future Utility: Global Combinatorial Optimization for Task-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
topic: KV cache compression / head-wise budget allocation / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 LU-KV; long-horizon marginal-utility optimization for head-wise KV budget allocation, reporting 80% KV-cache reduction with minimal degradation while reducing latency and GPU memory footprint.

title: Predictive Prefetching for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
topic: RAG serving / asynchronous retrieval / predictive prefetching / latency reduction
why: ICML 2026 RAG-serving acceleration; predicts when and what to retrieve before uncertainty peaks, reporting up to 43.5% lower end-to-end latency and 62.4% TTFT improvement while preserving answer quality.

title: Prefix-Cache-Aware Data Reordering for LLM-Augmented Database Analytics
topic: LLM serving / prefix KV-cache reuse / prompt-data layout / database analytics
why: ICML 2026 data-systems/LLM-serving work (SOLO) that reorders relational rows/columns to maximize reusable prompt prefixes; reports up to 90.3% higher prefill throughput and up to 242x lower planning overhead.

title: Preserve-Then-Quantize: Balancing Rank Budgets for Quantization Error Reconstruction in LLMs
topic: quantization / PTQ / low-rank reconstruction / QPEFT / low-bit LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists Preserve-Then-Quantize. Structured Residual Reconstruction preserves dominant activation-scaled singular directions before quantization and allocates remaining rank to error reconstruction, improving low-bit PTQ and 2-bit QPEFT accuracy under a fixed rank budget.

title: PRIM: Cooperative Dynamic Token Compression for Efficient Large Multimodal Models
topic: multimodal / MLLM inference / audio-video token compression / pruning / long-form multimodal efficiency
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads and the BUPT PESI official lab page confirm PRIM. It performs cooperative audio-video token compression across encoders and the language model using text-conditioned fusion, attention/frequency-aware pruning, and task-adaptive retention, reducing long-form multimodal inference FLOPs/latency while preserving accuracy.

title: Principled SVD-based Delta Compression via Quantization Error Minimization
topic: quantization / delta-model compression / multi-tenant LLM serving / storage efficiency / mixed precision
why: ICML 2026 Poster. PrinMix formulates SVD delta quantization as bit-budget-constrained optimization with reconstruction target correction, targeting storage and GPU-memory overhead of many fine-tuned LLM variants; reported results include over 6x storage savings and substantial accuracy gains over prior delta-compression baselines.

title: Prism-MoE: Efficient Dense-to-MoE Conversion for Visual Autoregressive Generation
topic: MoE systems / visual autoregressive generation / sparse activation / efficient model conversion
why: ICML 2026 Poster. Prism-MoE converts pretrained dense visual autoregressive generators into sparse MoE models using trajectory-consistent initialization and lightweight confidence-adaptive fine-tuning; reports dense-like generation quality with 37.5% active parameters and less than 10% of standard training budget.

title: Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusion Language Models
topic: efficient reasoning / diffusion language models / test-time scaling
why: ICML 2026 efficient test-time scaling for dLLMs; hierarchical trajectory search, partial remasking and self-verification match Best-of-N quality with substantially fewer function evaluations.

title: Prism: Spectral-Aware Block-Sparse Attention
topic: efficient attention / long-context prefill / Triton kernels
why: ICML 2026; training-free spectral-aware block-sparse attention with custom Triton kernels, reporting up to 5.1x speedup at 128K context with negligible accuracy loss.

title: Proact-VL: A Proactive VideoLLM for Real-Time AI Companions
topic: multimodal serving / streaming VideoLLM / real-time agent / low-latency inference / proactive response control
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Proact-VL targets continuous streaming VideoLLM deployment with low-latency inference, autonomous response triggering, and controllable generation under real-time constraints; Microsoft Research and the official project/repository confirm the ICML 2026 identity and real-time serving focus.

title: ProbMoE: Differentiable Probabilistic Routing for Mixture-of-Experts
topic: MoE systems/accelerators / dynamic routing / compute-efficient training and inference
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. ProbMoE formulates hard cardinality-constrained expert selection probabilistically and extends naturally to dynamic-k routing, allowing adaptive expert allocation while using fewer activated experts at comparable quality; official author project and repository are available.

title: ProphetKV: User-Query-Driven Selective Recomputation for Efficient KV Cache Reuse in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
topic: KV cache reuse / RAG serving / selective recomputation
why: ICML 2026 query-driven KV-cache reuse for RAG; dedicates recomputation budget to query-relevant tokens and reports 96-101% of full-prefill accuracy at only 20% recomputation while outperforming CacheBlend/EPIC/KVShare on RULER and LongBench.

title: Proteus: Lookup-Free Trellis-Coded Quantization by Lattice-Breaking Compute Codes for 2-Bit LLMs
topic: quantization / 2-bit weight-only PTQ / trellis-coded quantization / lookup-free dequantization / GPU memory traffic / LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 direct ultra-low-bit LLM inference work. Proteus replaces runtime codebook/LUT access in 2-bit trellis-coded quantization with compute-generated integer mixing plus affine Gaussianization, targeting the memory-traffic bottleneck of autoregressive decoding. The official repository describes CUDA dequantization kernels, profiling, and the end-to-end quantization pipeline.

title: ProtoKV: Streaming Video Understanding under Delayed Query with Summary-State Memory
topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / bounded KV memory / delayed-query inference / summary-state memory
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by the official ICML inventory. ProtoKV targets streaming-video inference with delayed asynchronous queries under fixed GPU-memory and latency budgets, retaining an exact near-window while compressing distant history into fixed-capacity semantic-spatial prototypes; it improves long-delay accuracy by up to 12.5 points over token-retention baselines at matched budgets.

title: Proxy Compression for Language Modeling
topic: language-model training efficiency / byte-level modeling / compressed training views
why: ICML 2026. Joint training on raw bytes and externally compressed proxy views retains a raw-byte inference interface while improving fixed-compute training efficiency; gains strengthen with scale and approach tokenizer-based models.

title: PsumQuant: In-line Post-training Partial Sum Quantizer for Energy Efficient NPU Inference

title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification
topic: VLA speculative inference / algorithm-architecture co-design
why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.

title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
topic: MoE serving / high-bandwidth flash architecture
why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
topic: MoE architecture / small-batch decoding
why: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have been widely adopted in real-time interactive applications such as coding assistants, real-time audio-video interaction systems. To meet the extremely low response latency requirements of these scenarios, practitioners commonly employ small-batch decoding, under which MoE inference becomes memory-bound and is severely bottlenecked by expert weight loading. However, this bottleneck has received limited attention, and existing solutions such as post-training weight compression or fine-grained expert design during pre-training either degrade model accuracy or introduce additional computation and communication overhead. To tackle this issue, we propose DeaMoE, a decoding-efficient MoE architecture, in which the experts are grouped into several departments, and the experts belonging to the same department share most parameters since they come from the same professional field, and additionally each expert contains a few private parameters to reflect its uniqueness. Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
topic: VLA device-edge co-inference / energy-aware runtime
why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference
topic: MoE memory-efficient W4A16 inference / GPU slot cache
why: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models reduce arithmetic by activating only a small subset of experts per token, yet deployment still requires storing and moving the full expert bank. We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.
